It is of the same provenance as the "modern versions" issued from "critical text" readings today. And like all modern versions, is designed to further the satanic "Yea, hath God said?" sowing of doubtful disputations.

There was never a BC translation of the Hebrew into Greek, other than some verses from the pentateuch. There was no letter, no 72 Israelite scholars. And Jesus and the Apostles did not "quote" from it. It was a Jewish lie from the beginning, adopted by the apostate church of Rome.

**Luke 24:44-45**
*And he said unto them, These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in **the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms**, concerning me. Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures*

Jesus, opening the disciples understanding of the scriptures, lays out precisely the format of the Old Testament, and excludes all other works that some claim to be scripture.

There is the Law of Moses, the Pentateuch - the first five books of the Bible, credited to Moses. The Prophets, the series of books telling the history of Israel through the prophets of God. And Psalms, the songs and Proverbs inspired by God. These are the oracles of God, the scripture that taught of Christ.

There was no mention of apocryphal books or texts, because they did not write of Him.

teachings.title: The Septuagint myth
teachings.summary: Argues that the story of 72 scholars translating the Septuagint in 250 BC has no evidence behind it, and that the LXX people cite today is Origen's own work.
teachings.text:
It is harder to take seriously people who think the "Septuagint" (or the "LXX" as it's called) was really compiled and translated by "72 Israelite scholars" 6 each from the "12 tribes," in 250BC than it is to take seriously those who accept the "Dead Sea Scrolls" as authoritative.

It was a creation of the apostate Origen, in the second century AD, filled with errors, contains later apocryphal works, and was used to justify heresies of gnostics in the early Roman Catholic cult.

Jesus cited the OT scripture, compiled in Hebrew by scribes of Levites, that He Himself had inspired. With jots and tittles.

The "Letter of Aristeas" that supposedly commissioned this work, appears to have been a forgery written by the Alexandrian apostate Jew, Philo, in the first century AD, to justify his heresies. The "12 tribes" did not exist in 250BC, and there were no scribes in among the long scattered and destroyed 10 tribes of the Northern Kingdom. There is no evidence of the existence of a Greek translation, other than a copy of Deuteronomy 23-28, with zero indication that it was from a larger work, and dated to 150BC, a century later than the supposed Septuagint.

When people today talk about the LXX they are not referring to a translation from 250BC, but are entirely talking about the second column of Origen's Hexapla, where his own translation was recorded.

teachings.title: The critical text and the preserved word
teachings.summary: Criticizes modern translations built on old but contradicting manuscripts over the preserved majority text.
teachings.text:
"Critical Text theologians," who support the modern translations, using corrupt, incomplete or contradicting text found on a scrap of parchment discovered in a cave, or minority texts in trash to be burned, and insist on their use being superior to the preserved majority text, because they are "older," think they are covered on the "*Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish ought from it*" clause.

That they have immunity.

It's similar in spirit to the Jews who put the copper wire around Manhattan. A talmudic Phariseeism that they can trick God.

They offer a passive aggressive means of corrupting God's word; "Hey, they aren't doing anything of the sort! They're simply using the oldest available text! It's a perfectly fair translation of those corrupt texts. Those verses are missing there, don't blame us!"

It is like the devil's inverted counterfeit version of God's preservation, except it relies on corrupt texts kept in a burn pile for centuries, riddled with errors, rather than a continuous passing down of unchanging word of God.

But they see karmic release in their trying to trick God. But they won't. *God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.*

It is the most arbitrary standard that could possibly exist. If they are "older," they are more reliable. If they've been kept from the knowledge of all men for centuries, then it doesn't matter what contradictions they create.

But they are sons of Belial. It's the devil's oldest trick; *Yea, hath God said?*

teachings.title: The Bible explains itself
teachings.summary: Notes that scripture interprets itself through parallels between the Old and New Testaments and that God is not the author of confusion.
teachings.text:
On the subject of parallelism in scripture, the best example of it is the Old Testament and New. The Bible explains itself, because God gives examples and parables and like manner of things to explain the spiritual. And then he will do it multiple times just to be sure we understand.

That's why people who say that interpreting the scriptures is difficult are showing that they're not saved. While there are passages that we see through a glass darkly, most of the truth of the word of God is readily available to those in the Spirit. God is not the author of confusion.

*But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.*

teachings.title: Modern versions drop "hunger" in John 6:35
teachings.summary: Points to the omission of hunger in the NIV and ESV against John 6:35 as a reason to read the Authorized Version, the preserved word of God.
teachings.text:
NIV: Earliest manuscripts and many other ancient sources don't include hunger.

NASB: ....

ESV: omitted - The earliest manuscripts do not include hunger


 If you aren't using the Authorized Version, referred to as the King James Bible, you aren't reading the preserved word of God. You will die of hunger

*And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.*

I seriously don't understand how people read the modern translations. The fact that they are all corrupt aside. They are horribly translated and the additions of the doubtful disputation footnotes and the letters and call outs and chapter titles...it's like comparing Shakespeare to Korean stereo instructions.

teachings.title: Building on the Rock: the word of God as final authority
teachings.summary: Says that Biblical fundamentalism is building on the Rock, Christ and the inspired, preserved word, and that trusting tradition or newfound manuscripts is building on sand.
teachings.text:
If you don't build your house upon the rock, that is the word of God; Inerrant. Preserved inspired perfect. And instead are trusting on traditions of men, with changing doctrine. Newfound translations and scraps of manuscripts turning up in caves, and various religious leaders who list to and fro as the wind blows, clouds without water... If that's you, you're building your house upon the sand.

*Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: and the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.*

All Biblical fundamentalism is simply building upon the Rock, that is Christ and God's word. Both literally in scripture, and in the sense that it is His promise, which we trust by faith.

*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*

That we have the whole word, inspired and preserved, that we have been promised so that we may live.

*But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.*

To be completely furnished to know everything, every doctrine, that we require to live a righteous life unto good works.

*All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: that the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.*

Those that reject these basic tenets of the faith do so by denying that all doctrine comes from scripture. That they reject the idea utterly.

It's built on sand.

teachings.title: The church fathers and the canon of scripture
teachings.summary: Explains that the church fathers are not final authorities, that they often disagreed with each other and with scripture, and urges believers to read them for themselves and test everything by scripture.
teachings.text:
And to criticism that I "pick and choose when to use the 'church fathers,'" my point in linking this Twitter thread that demolishes the idea that the canon of scripture that God gave us and preserved for all time, (sufficiently available to men in every age to bring them to righteousness, and testified as truth in the Spirit) isn't to say that the 'church fathers' are final authorities, but that if your entire theology is based on the traditions of men, you may want to actually know what they said, and acknowledge that they disagree with your modern understandings that you lean so heavily on.

I don't need brother Polycarp to tell me what the Spirit does.

In short; believe the Gospel. Read scripture for doctrine. Find a good church that preaches the whole word of God and sings Psalms and hymns right with doctrine.

And if you want to read early writings of first and second century Christians, by all means do so. Just don't rely on other men to tell you what they said, read them yourself. And with everything, search the scriptures to see if what they wrote is so. They were just men and are fallible, after all. But all knowledge and wisdom comes from God, through the Holy Spirit.

The modern internet theologian takes the route of trusting what they are told was the position of "church fathers," when the cited authors often disagreed with not only each other, but with scripture, or agreed with scripture but are contradicted by modern theologies. There is no discernment exercised.

They place all "church fathers" on the same level, cherry pick what doctrines to take from them, often defend their doctrines by citing men who actually held opposing positions, and never compare spiritual things to spiritual things allowing the Bible to tell them what doctrine should be. Most of the time it's because they are themselves unsaved. And the natural man receiveth not the things of God. They are spiritually discerned.

teachings.title: Understanding Scripture by the Indwelling Spirit
teachings.summary: Reminds that the saved have the Holy Spirit to give understanding of His word, that no mediator or priest is needed except Jesus, and that the natural man cannot understand it.
teachings.text:
Reminder: the Bible says that if you be saved, that you have the Holy Spirit within you to guide you and give you wisdom and knowledge and understanding of His word. All knowledge comes from the Lord. We have no need for any mediator between God and man except Jesus. We are a holy priesthood.

You do not need a third party. Intermediary to explain to you biblical doctrines. You do not need a priest, in fact, the New Testament explicitly speaks out against it. The pastor acts as a bishop, a shepherd to their flock. They can lead and guide but the Bible is the final authority.

Cults tell you that you need a man to explain scripture to you. God doesn't hide His wisdom. There is no gnostic revelation.

If you struggle understanding the Bible yourself, read it more and pray for wisdom. And if you're not saved by faith alone then you're a natural man and unable to understand it. Simple as.

teachings.title: Making an Idol of the Translation, a Man or an Opinion
teachings.summary: Warns that elevating the KJV translation above the God who gave the word, or following a man or an opinion as an identity, is a form of idolatry.
teachings.text:
It struck me the other day when Ruckmanites were arguing that the KJV, which is the inspired and preserved whole word of God in English, providentially collected and translated at the dawn of English being the lingua franca of the world, and the printing press and universal literacy, was more than that, but itself to be seen as a separate inspiration, given to the translators. Implying the book itself was different and special and thus the preservation of the word to that point, wasn't. That God's word hasn't been preserved for all ages in the manner He saw fit and necessary to save those who would answer the call, but only in 1611 became perfect.

This makes the translation itself an idol. It is worshiping the created more than the Creator who spake it into existence before all creation, and Whose Spirit overcame the prophets and apostles to reveal it. And the defense of the man or men who promote this idea to the point of infallibility is Idolatry.

All the "I am of Apollos," "I am of Paul," "I am of Catholicism," "I am of Luther," "Calvin," "Hyles," "MacArthur," "Ruckman," "Anderson"... whomever, not necessarily a reflection of the man, but the need by others to make the man or their ideas your identity, is a form of Idolatry too.

We recognize this form of idol worship in politicians and political movements, ideologies, and it's easy to spot in sin, Mammon, coveting things, but we often fail to see it when talking about the things of God as if they were more than the creature God made for His purpose.

The clay more than the potter.

And so, rather than praising God that His word is there for us in our native tongue that we may be easily and thoroughly furnished to good works for Him, we can slip into holding up the carnal, the clay as an idol itself.

**Colossians 3:5**
*Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry*

**Isaiah 44**

*9 They that make a graven image are all of them vanity; and their delectable things shall not profit; and they are their own witnesses; they see not, nor know; that they may be ashamed.

10 Who hath formed a god, or molten a graven image that is profitable for nothing?

11 Behold, all his fellows shall be ashamed: and the workmen, they are of men: let them all be gathered together, let them stand up; yet they shall fear, and they shall be ashamed together.

12 The smith with the tongs both worketh in the coals, and fashioneth it with hammers, and worketh it with the strength of his arms: yea, he is hungry, and his strength faileth: he drinketh no water, and is faint.

13 The carpenter stretcheth out his rule; he marketh it out with a line; he fitteth it with planes, and he marketh it out with the compass, and maketh it after the figure of a man, according to the beauty of a man; that it may remain in the house.

14 He heweth him down cedars, and taketh the cypress and the oak, which he strengtheneth for himself among the trees of the forest: he planteth an ash, and the rain doth nourish it.

15 Then shall it be for a man to burn: for he will take thereof, and warm himself; yea, he kindleth it, and baketh bread; yea, he maketh a god, and worshippeth it; he maketh it a graven image, and falleth down thereto.

16 He burneth part thereof in the fire; with part thereof he eateth flesh; he roasteth roast, and is satisfied: yea, he warmeth himself, and saith, Aha, I am warm, I have seen the fire:

17 And the residue thereof he maketh a god, even his graven image: he falleth down unto it, and worshippeth it, and prayeth unto it, and saith, Deliver me; for thou art my god.

18 They have not known nor understood: for he hath shut their eyes, that they cannot see; and their hearts, that they cannot understand.

19 And none considereth in his heart, neither is there knowledge nor understanding to say, I have burned part of it in the fire; yea, also I have baked bread upon the coals thereof; I have roasted flesh, and eaten it: and shall I make the residue thereof an abomination? shall I fall down to the stock of a tree?

20 He feedeth on ashes: a deceived heart hath turned him aside, that he cannot deliver his soul, nor say, Is there not a lie in my right hand?*

teachings.title: Italicized Words and the Preservation of the KJV
teachings.summary: Uses the italicized words of 1 John 2:23 and their witness in ancient manuscripts and early Bibles as an example of God's preservation, and argues that going back to the Greek cannot correct the KJV.
teachings.text:
Funner fact: The last ten words of 1 John 2:23 that are in italics in the KJV (which don't change doctrine but reaffirm the statement being made) were also found in the Old Latin manuscripts, the Syriac, the Coptic, Armenian, Ethiopic and the Latin Vulgate, Martin Luther's German Bible 1545, the Spanish Sagradas Escrituras of 1569, the Italian Diodati of 1649, and the Cipriano de Valera of 1602. They are included in Wycliffe 1395, in the Greek texts of Beza, Scrivener and Elzevir.

The italicized words can also be found in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Psi, C, 33, 614, 630, 1505, 1739 and many other majority text manuscripts, as well as being quoted by Origen, Athanasius, Cyril, Cyprian and Hilary.

God's word was spoken by Him before all creation and preserved by Him for all time, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: that the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.

FUN FACT: The last ten words of 1 John 2:23 in your King James Bible are italicized.

The point is that the italicized words appearing in the King James Bible, which is the preserved inspired word of God in English, is an example of God's *preservation* of that which He inspired, breathed. Spoke. Before the foundation of the world.

I am King James only because it is the perfect and preserved word of God in English. My native tongue. What a blessing that is.

But what is important is the content not the container. We should never lose sight of that.

The critical text reading intellectuals who insist that you have to go back to the Greek to get the true meaning of scripture, fetishizing the language or how old the manuscripts are are no different than the Hebrew roots fools who think they have to use yeshua as Jesus' name because it sounds exotic and different.

If you're a native English speaker, you can find all the doctrine you need in the King James Bible. And there is no other name under heaven but Jesus by which we can be saved.

So unless you're a native Greek speaker or native Hebrew speaker it's foolishness

But again the point is going back to the Greek can't correct the KJV but neither can the KJV correct the Greek for God's word has been preserved for all time.

God's preserved word would be the same in Martian if such a thing were possible.

teachings.title: God's Word: Inspired, Preserved and the Living Word
teachings.summary: Shows that God's word has always been revealed and preserved regardless of language or format, warns against men who sow doubt about it and false gospels, and leads into Jesus as the Word of God in Revelation 19.
teachings.text:
*It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.*

**1 Corinthians 2**

*But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit: for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God. For what man knoweth the things of a man, save the spirit of man which is in him? even so the things of God knoweth no man, but the Spirit of God.

Now we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the spirit which is of God; that we might know the things that are freely given to us of God. Which things also we speak, not in the words which man's wisdom teacheth, but which the Holy Ghost teacheth; comparing spiritual things with spiritual.

But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned. But he that is spiritual judgeth all things, yet he himself is judged of no man. For who hath known the mind of the Lord, that he may instruct him? But we have the mind of Christ.*

The Bible says God's word always was, has been revealed in all creation, written in our hearts, shown by the wrath of nature, spoken through inspiration by the prophets, given by inspiration to the same, recorded in different languages via different medium over the ages, preached in different tongues by the power of the Holy Ghost and by the God-given talents of pastors, evangelists and translators, perfect and complete, that no man may have an excuse. Good for doctrine and instruction on righteousness that a man may be thoroughly furnished. That is, completely equipped, to understand the will of God and the faith by which we can be saved.

The sheep hear His voice.

It isn't about how it is physically presented, what language it is in, the punctuation or capitalisation, idioms and vagaries of transliteration. The doctrines and spiritual intent remains pure, preserved by God for all time. It is His promise and His testimony. Oral or written in stone, parchment, book or on a screen. Said from a pulpit or at someone's door. Because it is written in our hearts, and given by the Holy Spirit who gives all knowledge and wisdom.

People get caught up in the worldly details, distracted by pedantic, carnal things. But we are given wisdom by God through the Spirit, revealed in His word that we can live by. Perfect for all time. Preserved by His almighty providence.

Amen.

This all is important as we move to **Revelation 19**, where we are told one of the names of Jesus is the Word of God. Capital W.

It is important to understanding that the entire scripture is given as a testimony by God of His promise, fulfilled in Christ. It is that faith in those promises, believing the report of Christ and salvation, redemption in the blood, the resurrection and the kingdom, that grants us eternal life. Since Adam. Since man called upon the name of the Lord. Right through to the end.

Jesus is the living Word of God made flesh. The Alpha and Omega. Who in the beginning was with God and is God. Slain before the foundation of the world.

If there is a supposed pastor who teaches another Gospel, multiple ways to salvation, then they are accursed. Calling them reprobate is in line with Biblical teaching.

*As we said before, so say I now again, If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.*

This is not accusing anyone who has differences on secondary doctrine or interpretation of more obscure text and prophecy, but literally those bringing a false witness to a false Gospel along with other heresies for the express purpose of leading men astray, creating apostates and worse, while calling themselves men of God. Just as Jesus gave us instruction regarding false teachers;

 *Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles? Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit. A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit. Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire. Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them.*

People get caught up in cults of men rather than spiritual things, and allowing God's word to instruct us, in the Spirit.

God's word is inspired for all time. Preserved for all time.

And men who make a living by making merchandise off of those who fall into their snares, by perverting God's word, for coming up with earthly theories about carnal things such as what language a translation is in or how linguistic transliteration may differ, semantics and nonsense, to make people doubt His word and its preservation, are wicked as Hell.

The Greek texts and the KJV agree. If your concordances and margin notes and footnotes show disagreement, it's because they are not the inspired and preserved word of God, not because the source or translation is corrupt.

If you have to "go back to the Greek" to sell a doctrine to English speakers that you can't sell them on with the KJV, it isn't there.

And if you claim the English is not only different and superior, you agree with the critical text apostates who don't believe in God's preservation of His word, just coming at it from another angle.

Perfect.
Inspired.
Preserved.
True.

teachings.title: The Word of God Inspired and Preserved
teachings.summary: Strings together scripture to show that God inspired and preserved His words for all time, available in English in the King James Version.
teachings.text:
The word of God is inspired and preserved for all time. The same since before creation. Perfect. Complete. Preserved.
God breathed.
God preserved.

And it is available to us who speak and read English in the King James Version.

*The words of the Lord are pure words: as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times. Thou shalt keep them, O Lord, thou shalt preserve them from this generation for ever.*

*God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds.

 In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God.

As for me, this is my covenant with them, saith the LORD; My spirit that is upon thee, and my words which I have put in thy mouth, shall not depart out of thy mouth, nor out of the mouth of thy seed, nor out of the mouth of thy seed's seed, saith the LORD, from henceforth and for ever.
*
As for God, his way is perfect: The word of the LORD is tried: He is a buckler to all those that trust in him.

*He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he.*

*It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by **every** word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.*

The same yesterday, today and forever. Amen.

And all who say it hasn't been inspired and preserved for all time are calling God a liar.

*The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand for ever.*

Amen

teachings.title: Faith cometh by hearing, and rightly dividing the word
teachings.summary: Says critics of biblical fundamentalism take symbols literally while denying plain scripture, and explains that God's word is the means by which the Gospel converts souls however it is communicated. Notes that even believers can fall into traps when they fail to rightly divide the word, as over whether one must call on the Lord's name to be saved.
teachings.text:
I often find people like this who call biblical fundamentalism too literal, failed to understand the spiritual aspect of scripture and themselves take what is symbolic or a picture of other things and draw literal interpretations from them while denying clear scripture that means exactly what it says.

Most aren't saved.

In this case, the Bible says that Faith cometh by hearing and hearing by the word of God. The emphasis here is on the scriptures being used as the means of conveying the Gospel to the lost. The Bible has power. God's word is used to convert souls. How God's word is communicated to a person, most commonly audibly, is irrelevant to the fact that it is God's word that brings about faith in a person. Only a fool would take it to mean that the deaf can't get saved. It's just as foolish as saying the mute can't be saved because they can't call upon the name of the Lord.

Some who are saved fall into similar spiritual traps by not being able to rightly divide the word of God. There's a rift in believers I know over whether you have to actually call upon the name of the Lord to be saved, rather than just believe in your heart. It becomes a semantic and autistic spiral of foolish assertions, and dividing the word of God takes a backseat to silly hypotheticals.

Anyway, the so-called "doctor of divinity" in this tweet thread is an unsaved viper teaching that you can save people with your own words, or actions, rather than God's word and Christ's actions. It's wicked and no wonder he makes such a stupid defense of it.

teachings.title: The natural man and the spirit of the parables
teachings.summary: Quotes Psalm 19:1-7 and teaches that Jesus' parables and figures, such as bread, flesh, blood and the gate, are spiritual and are misread by the natural man who takes them literally, like Nicodemus. Notes that this world will pass away and serves as a schoolmaster to bring us to the truth.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 19:1-7**
*The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.

Day unto day uttereth speech, and night unto night sheweth knowledge. There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard. Their line is gone out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world. In them hath he set a tabernacle for the sun, Which is as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber, and rejoiceth as a strong man to run a race.

His going forth is from the end of the heaven, and his circuit unto the ends of it: and there is nothing hid from the heat thereof. The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.*

**Romans 1:18-20**
*For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them.

For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse.*

It's important to understand that all of creation exists to teach us about God, and salvation in Jesus Christ.

People misunderstand the nature of parables in the Bible. They think that when Jesus uses parables of things we are familiar with, be it sowing seeds and harvesting fruit, or the living water or the bread of life, shepherds and sheep... It is to use the familiar natural things to teach us the spiritual, and it's true. But they don't understand that nature IS this way specifically to serve as that example. That God made all of creation to serve as a living parable.

Sound. Light. Food. Plants. Animals. Seasons. Marriage. Childbirth. Stars. Sun and moon. Literally everything in creation is there to teach us the ways of God.

The natural man receiveth not the things of God for they are spiritually discerned.

When Jesus uses the parables He actually set up, from before creation, to be part of His word, they confound those unwilling to hear, unable to see. Hearts hardened, they take His meaning literally, as the thing itself rather than the spirit with which it's meant.

*It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.*

And so when He speaks of bread, and eating His flesh, and drinking His blood, and the waters of Life and that he is the gate, that He is the shepherd, that man must be born again to enter the kingdom of Heaven, all of this is Spirit. It is parable. And the things He uses as examples exist so that they may serve that purpose.

Those who take it literally, carnally, like Nicodemus, are incapable of understanding the spiritual application for all things.

This world will pass away. Heaven and earth will be rolled up like a scroll. None of this will last and is incidental outside of serving as a school master to bring us to the truth of God.

teachings.title: God promised to preserve His words
teachings.summary: Points to Psalm 12:6-7, where God promises to keep and preserve His pure words for ever, as the reason modern versions alter that passage.
teachings.text:
It is clear why modern perversions of the Bible change Psalm 12, where God promises to preserve His word for all time.

*The words of the Lord are pure words: as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times. Thou shalt keep them, O Lord, thou shalt preserve them from this generation for ever.*

teachings.title: Conscience and testing the doctrines of men
teachings.summary: Says the conscience is the law written in the heart and a sign that we need salvation, and that the seared conscience of reprobates is silent. Gives a way to test doctrines of men by comparing them to known scripture, and asks that disagreements over secondary doctrine stay civil.
teachings.text:
I think the idea of angels on your shoulder came from the way people move their eyes when asked a question. People with a conscience, anyway.

A conscience is the law written in our heart, and something the Bible says is a way God reveals Himself to us. A physical manifestation of our knowing we need salvation for our sin, written on the face of a person trapped in it. That tinge of the heart telling us that Satan is already accusing us of whatever it is, before God, right at that moment. It hits even harder when you're saved and should know better. New man and the Spirit taking over the role the angel of conscience had, and God's rod of correction replacing the devil.

Psychopath reprobates don't have that problem, their conscience seared as scripture says, and so they can lie with a straight face and no guilt. All they have is the devil whispering in their ear.

If you want to understand the things of God, learn His word and then consider the implications of each doctrine, and the patterns that each creates with the others. Just morality and the need for the law to prove to us we need saving, and how it provides the criteria for accepting the testimony of God, regarding Christ, by which we are saved for believing, and then ponder how that has played out in the Biblical history and in your own life...it's awesome

teachings.title: Biblical fundamentalism and the Trinity
teachings.summary: Says the fundamentalist stops where scripture presents mystery, as with 1 John 5:7 and Colossians 2:1-4, rather than supplying philosophical machinery to explain the Godhead.
teachings.text:
Seeing people debate the various vain philosophy of men used to explain the position of the Father, the godhood of the incarnate Jesus, the Trinity, the person of the Spirit and the unity of it all, in the fallible and weakness of men's terms.

Biblical fundamentalism is superior to theology. Heresy answered with heresy is not how we find the truth.

It is by the revelation of scripture and understanding that some things our finite brain cannot comprehend. And accepting those things by faith.

Where the text of scripture presents mystery, “*great is the mystery of godliness*, ” the fundamentalist stops, where the philosopher and the theologian continue, pressing on in their vain imagination.

The fundamentalist does not feel obligated to supply the missing metaphysical machinery that finite minds invent to close the gap. And we don't need to take sides in the back-and-forth debates of differing heretical schools of thought.

Way too many Christians, saved, bible-believing Christians at that, see an answer to a clear heresy that is closer to the truth, and accept that doctrine as solid. They lean on the understanding of traditions. The consensus of the crowd.

Fundamentalists should never accept presuppositions and systematics that require us to adopt a set of beliefs that come prepackaged, regurgitating apologetics because others before us accepted them whole cloth.

Always search the scripture to see if it is so. And if you cannot draw a clear, direct understanding of a doctrine or view from plain language and context, then it is ok and in fact wise, to leave it to faith and admit your ignorance as fallible, finite man.

The fundamentalist rejects the theologian's "Sola scriptura," for pure Bible. They use the logic of men, the writings of church fathers and reformers and past generations of men to claim the Bible should be the final arbiter of doctrine. That sliver of daylight given to the authority of tradition and man's philosophy, invites error just as much as the other attempts to answer bad doctrine.

Taking scripture compared to scripture as the only means of finding truth, and allowing the Bible to be the only authority for matters of faith and practice, avoids these traps.

And the general understanding of Romans 14, that on secondary matters, men may disagree and be persuaded themselves, without judging another man's servant, makes fundamentalism the way. Primary doctrine is clear. God is not the author of confusion. But where we see through a glass darkly there is room for brotherly disagreement.

**1 John 5:7**
*For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one.*

The Bible does not demand that we figure out the metaphysical mechanics of how three can be one. It simply states the fact of their heavenly record and their absolute unity, leaving no room for human rationalization.

Scripture doesn't get into the mode, essence or hypostatic union or the filioque or any other nonsense used to debate endlessly the vain wisdom of man.

It identifies them by their revealed biblical names: Father, Word, and Holy Ghost, and the undeniable fact that these three are one.



1 John 5:6
*This is he that came by water and blood, even Jesus Christ; not by water only, but by water and blood. And it is the Spirit that beareth witness, because the Spirit is truth.*

God anchors the reality of Jesus Christ to historical facts, He was born of water, the incarnation, and he came by blood, the death and resurrection. And the person of the Spirit bears witness to Christ's factual existence and the truth of the gospel.

There is no need to explain what we know is true. It is just true.

Verse 9, *If we receive the witness of men, the witness of God is greater: for this is the witness of God which he hath testified of his Son.*

The theologian and the seminarian and the other "experts," seek to gain our confidence in them. In their arguments and their theories and their jargon.

But the witness of God is greater.

Verse 10 *He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son.*

We have the Spirit of truth, Who teaches us all things. Who does not speak of Himself, but the good things of God.

**1 Corinthians 2:12–13**
*Now we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the spirit which is of God; that we might know the things that are freely given to us of God. Which things also we speak, not in the words which man’s wisdom teacheth, but which the Holy Ghost teacheth; comparing spiritual things with spiritual.*

What more do we need? And this truth speaks expressly of the truth we have known and the gift of eternal life that we may know Him. The truth that is the true God.

**1 John 5:20**
*And we know that the Son of God is come, and hath given us an understanding, that we may know him that is true, and we are in him that is true, even in his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God, and eternal life.*

So don't let theologians and men wise in their own conceits tell you that you need to be "educated" as they are to know the truth.

God Himself testifies with us the truth of His Son. Amen.

**Colossians 2:1–4**
*For I would that ye knew what great conflict I have for you, and for them at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh; That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love, and unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the acknowledgement of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ; In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.

And this I say, lest any man should beguile you with enticing words.*

The beguiling men with enticing words seek to lead us from the truth. Paul in the Spirit is giving prophecy that applies to Christians today as much as it did the Colossians and the Laodiceans.

Our hearts may be comforted with the assurance of full understanding, even as we acknowledge the mystery of God. Of the Father and of Christ and ALL of the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.

**Colossians 2:6–9**
*As ye have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk ye in him: Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith, as ye have been taught, abounding therein with thanksgiving. Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ. For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily.*

We have received Christ, sealed by the Spirit in Jesus, we are rooted in Him. We are called to walk in Him, and because we are established in the faith, secure in our knowledge of the truth, we can never deny Him, but we can be spoiled by deceivers. Led away by vain traditions of men, following the ways of the world, the logic of men. Following the theology and theory and disputations of denomination and schools of thought, instead of Christ.

The fulness of the Godhead is stated as a fact, *in* Christ. The scripture does not seek to define His "essence," substance, or the mechanics of that fulness. God's word simply declares it, its truth, and then warns against the very methods that later generations of men would use to elaborate it. Their philosophy, traditions of men, and the rudimentary or elementary principles of the world. The natural man view.

The vain and puffed up philosophy, groups of men with creeds and confessions that add to and take away the things of Christ, teaching for commandments the doctrines of men.

**Colossians 2:16–18**
*Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ. Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels, intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind*

These are the tip of the iceberg, the various ways false teachers use their own imagination to invent how we should live, what we should do, and condemning those of us who place our trust entirely with Christ and His word.

teachings.title: No doctrine on a parable alone
teachings.summary: Fools misuse parables, and no doctrine should stand on a parable alone, as with Abraham's bosom, since Lazarus was carried to Abraham in heaven, not to a paradise compartment in hell.
teachings.text:
Just as the lame struggle to walk, the fool will misuse parables to their own purposes, drawing wrong conclusions and clouding understanding, rather than gaining wisdom.

While God uses parables throughout the Bible, Jesus teaching almost exclusively in parable to the hard-hearted Jews, so many have been used to create false doctrine. Proper application of parables should lay primarily on any explanation given in the text, (Jesus would often expound to the Apostles their meaning) but for those without clear teaching, the context should then be drawn by comparing scripture with scripture. No doctrine should stand alone on a parable.

The most obvious example is the false doctrine of "Abraham's bosom,' taken from **Luke 16's** tale of the rich man and Lazarus. Jesus is using their example to convey a message of urgency to the Jews, to repent and believe the gospel before its too late. To say that the prophets and Moses gave witness to His day, harken to them and believe. That those who don't are Hell-bound, no matter how rich they are. That those with dull ears and blind eyes will not believe, even if one were to raise from the dead.

But that the faithful, even the afflicted and poor in this world, who call upon the name of the Lord, are carried by angels into Heaven, honored and seated with Abraham, the father of faith. To be comforted forever.

The eisegesis and natural man logic required to turn this simple (and I believe, true) story into a doctrine that says that there is a place in Hell that's actually a compartment containing paradise, called "Abraham's bosom," and that that's where Old Testament saints went, is absurd.

The embrace of Abraham is specifically to show how even the lowly beggar, covered in sores, whose life was misery and rejection, someone lower than the dogs without the rich man's gate, rejected by the respecters of persons Jesus is addressing, is given an honor that Jews would be envious of. To sit down with Abraham, in the paradise that is God's heavenly kingdom.

As vs 9 says; *As a thorn goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouths of fools.*

teachings.title: The mark of the beast and adding to scripture
teachings.summary: Says taking the mark of the beast requires worshipping the beast and his image, and that Revelation 22:18-19 warns those who add to or take from scripture.
teachings.text:
Taking the Mark of The Beast requires one to worship the beast and his image.

*For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect...And he causeth all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond, to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads...And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet that wrought miracles before him, with which he deceived them that had received the mark of the beast, and them that worshipped his image. These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone....And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them: and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.*

No one who is saved will worship the beast to take his mark. No person who takes the mark will repent and be saved, they are blotted out of the book of life, the Bible says. Reprobates. Rejected of God.

Beware false prophets who seek to tell you that there is no such thing as being given up for holding the truth in unrighteousness. Who say you can be forgiven for blasphemy of the holy Spirit, when Jesus says there is no forgiveness for it. That there aren't reprobates, when the Jews who hardened their hearts were damned, unable to hear the truth and be healed.

Finally, **Revelation 22:18-19** is clear; anyone who adds to scripture or takes away from scripture is blotted out of the book of life, and accursed.

*For I testify unto every man that heareth the words of the prophecy of this book, If any man shall add unto these things, God shall add unto him the plagues that are written in this book: And if any man shall take away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God shall take away his part out of the book of life, and out of the holy city, and from the things which are written in this book.*

Jesus Christ Himself testifies that this is true. His last command in the final chapter of the final book of the Bible.

No one is ever written into the book of life once they've been removed.

teachings.title: Blessed are they that do his commandments
teachings.summary: Revelation 22:14 is Jesus' present exhortation to the saved, not a demand for works in eternity, where the curse is lifted.
teachings.text:
**Revelation 22:14**
*Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.*

This verse from the last chapter of the Bible, after John is wrapped up the revelation of Jesus Christ, pulled out of context to claim that in the new Heaven and new Earth we're going to need to do works to stay saved or something....wew. You know, after the resurrection after the glorified bodies after putting on incorruption after receiving that hope... Now we got to start doing works? LOL ok.

Context matters.

**Revelation 22:1-5**
*And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb. In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations. And there shall be no more curse: but the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it; and his servants shall serve him: And they shall see his face; and his name shall be in their foreheads. And there shall be no night there; and they need no candle, neither light of the sun; for the Lord God giveth them light: and they shall reign for ever and ever.*

This is the final prophecy for what it will be like in eternity. The curse is lifted. Every man and woman who was saved by faith will be healed and forever be with Christ, amen. What a glorious day.

Imagine trying to then add works, to place that curse of the law back upon us in perfection.

What a wicked thing.

Meanwhile, verses 10-16 are not describing the future. They are Jesus' message to the present. Encouraging we who are saved to keep His commandants, amen.

*I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches.*

People who wrest with scripture, using out of context verses and saying "it may not say this crazy thing, but it is implied!" are always undone by the word of God.

teachings.title: Ruckmanism: serpent seed, the Gap Theory and the KJV
teachings.summary: Rejects Peter Ruckman's teachings, such as serpent seed, UFOs and Jews saved by works, while holding the KJV as God's preserved word without correcting it from the Greek. Goes through his errors one by one: serpent seed, demons, UFOs, Jesus able to sin, "advanced revelation" in the KJV, and the Gap Theory from Scofield.
teachings.text:
Ruckman taught another gospel. It is wicked and accursed and all his other teachings that flowed from it were wicked and blasphemous and did not come from the KJV Bible. UFOs and new Adams on alien planets and the kingdom given to unbelieving Jews who were saved by works....all of it is evil. The divorces and the fruit of his ministry, wicked preachers who teach "Serpent Seed" and other wicked doctrine only adds to it.

I don't care if you think he was right about the KJV (it's a perverted twisting of sound doctrine IMO), it cannot overcome his insane teachings.

Imagine being correct that the KJV is the only Bible today we need and then being so spiritually blind that you pull damnable heresy from your own vain imagination instead of the rock of the word you supposedly champion.

Good natured disagreement on the topic between brothers is fine, and there are many great pastors today who hold similar views on the providential nature of the beautiful Authorized Version. And while some could nitpick their opinions, God bless them for their standards and doctrines. Their fruit is a consistent gospel and soul-winning flocks, amen.

Lots of good pastors out there are wrong on one secondary doctrine or opinion. Hard not to be when Bible colleges and seminaries are out there, teaching for commandments the doctrines of men (especially around the Jews and the end times).

But praise God those things shake out in the wash. Meanwhile, we all share an every word Bible, the blood of Jesus Christ and a great commission. Amen.

And I thank God Pastor Hyles stopped a bad habit he apparently had, of using the Greek to "correct" the King James.

His moderate position bridges the gap between two extremes and his defense of the Bible his momma gave him is the sweetest KJVO testimony you'd ever need.

It means guilt by association with things that no sane believer would want to be linked with, and isn't fair.

Serpent Seed and UFOs aren't being argued. In good faith, that label shouldn't be used unless they explicitly claim the whole mantle of Ruckman, or doctrines outside the stated topic of the wonderful Authorized Version.

Ruckman taught that Satan had sexual relations with Eve, resulting in the birth of Cain, a doctrine known as the serpent seed or dual-seed theory. This is detailed in his works, such as The Ruckman Reference Bible (first edition, p. 9) and The Book of Genesis (1969, p. 101-102, 118), where he suggests Genesis 3:15 implies Satan's seed, referencing 1 John 3:12 and John 8:44. He claimed this was "implied" rather than explicitly stated, but it lacks biblical foundation, contradicting Genesis 4:1, which explicitly states Adam fathered Cain.

Cain was given by God the choice to correct his works-based sacrifice. He chose not to, and slew his brother and reprobated himself. By making him into a literal child of Satan, it removes the entire point of free will and faith given in the story.

But if you teach that Adam and Eve were saved by works, that the Israelites were saved by works, and that the Millennium Kingdom will see a return to salvation by works, as the unbelieving Jews inheritance of the Kingdom hinges upon it, there's little constraining you to getting your doctrine solely from the inspired KJV, no matter how hard you protest for the Authorized Version.

Abortion is murder, life doesn't begin at the first breath. The blood of the innocent is upon the nation that tolerates and encourages the murder of babies, in the womb or out.

Saved Christians cannot be possessed by demons or devils, and absolutely no one has any Bible-based reason to claim they know what demons look like (He described demons as small, winged creatures resembling flies or mosquitoes (Demons and Christians, 1976) and admitted to his own personal demon possession.)

Eve did not have sex with the snake, and the apple wasn't an allegory for it. (And Adam, biting the same apple implies some disgusting abominations.) Cain was Adam's son according to the word of God. Also, Adam did not have water for blood according to any version of scripture, despite what Ruckman taught.

Ruckman believed UFOs were real, involving aliens with different blood types (e.g., black aliens with green blood, grey aliens with clear blood) and tied them to end-times events. He claimed the U.S. government collaborated with aliens, kidnapping citizens for experiments (Black Is Beautiful, 1996, pp. 230, 244, 291, 295-297, 310-311). He also suggested demons transport humans to other planets to “replenish” them (The Unknown Bible, 1984, p. 592).

Ruckman insisted that Jesus could have sinned. This is more of sophistry and foolishness than the other strange doctrines he held. Jesus being tempted at all points as we are, yet without sin is the biblical doctrine.

"Oh yeah, but He could have if He wants to!" is just dumb.

Ruckman held that biblical inspiration pertains to speaking, not writing, again a weird and unnecessary assertion that ignores the sundry times and diverse manner God has spoken to us.

Ruckman claimed the KJV provides “advanced revelation” superior to the original Hebrew and Greek texts. Some would argue this position with examples from the text.

He did not. He claimed advanced revelation from the KJV taught him that the antichrist is a 10-ft. tall alien with a bad right arm, a bad right eye, landing in St. Peter’s Square in a flying saucer 600 feet in diameter and 60 feet thick, and implanting the mark of the beast with his "huge black lips."

He claimed that the KJV translators were being given an advanced prophecy in **Numbers 33:52**

*Then ye shall drive out all the inhabitants of the land from before you, and destroy all their **pictures**, and destroy all their molten images, and quite pluck down all their high places*

That choosing to use "pictures" for images, they were warning us about TV and photography being evil, without them even knowing it. Bizarre.

In The Christian’s Handbook of Manuscript Evidence, Ruckman cited the rendering "churches" in **Acts 19:37**, when the Greek refers to "temples," as an advanced revelation, suggesting deeper spiritual insight not found in the Greek. What that insight is isn't immediately clear. Since it was regarding the building where an assembly gathers to worship (here a pagan assembly at that), church is the Modern English choice they used. Ok. What deeper meaning is there? Shrug.

He claimed typos and mistakes in the 1611 were of the Spirit, and not of the printers. He claimed that Easter was a pagan celebration, and ignored the 1611 containing a table to help Christians find the right date for Easter (Pascha) forever. Minds blown.

Ultimately, he did what false teachers do. Bait the hook with some truth, and then reel folks in with absolute insane nonsense.

Sheep's clothing. Appearance of righteousness. Etc.

It is this legacy that has done more damage to the cause of KJV onlyism in modern English speaking nations, by tainting that truth, than anyone who says the Antioch manuscripts and Masoretic Text used by the translators are equal to the KJV in inspiration, preservation and power.

Hope this helps explain my position.

This was going to just be a comment in the chat, but it's worthy of a post. "The Gap Theory" heresy.

Peter Ruckman taught the Gap Theory, asserting a time gap between Genesis 1:1 and 1:2, during which a pre-Adamic world, possibly involving Lucifer’s fall, was destroyed and left “without form, and void.” He discussed this in The Bible Babel (1964, p. 31) and The Book of Genesis (1970, pp. 11-16), citing support from heretic Clarence Larkin’s Dispensational Truth. The claim is that the geological record and "science" had to be reconciled to the Biblical 6 day creation. That since modern science had "debunked the Bible," they needed to make up absolute nonsense to square scripture to "reality."

The Gap Theory stems from Scofield, and his first note in his incredibly destructive reference Bible.

**Genesis 1:2**
*And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters*.

Scofield’s Margin Note (Genesis 1:2): “The earth was without form, and void: Jer. 4:23-26; Isa. 24:1; 45:18 clearly indicate that the earth had undergone a cataclysmic change as the result of a divine judgment. How about the world conform to the word of God? How about that?

teachings.title: Daniel 7 and the Revelation

teachings.text:

teachings.title: The stone cut out without hands
teachings.summary: The empires of Nebuchadnezzar's image came to pass, and Christ is the stone that breaks them and the head of the corner, so we cannot doubt God's promises.
teachings.text:
Now **Daniel 2** is a familiar story. King Nebuchadnezzar has a dream that troubles him, and he cannot recall what it was, but seeks someone to tell him the dream and its meaning.

And all the wizards and wise men of Chaldea cannot do this impossible task. The king orders that all his advisors be put to death for their inability to do this, including Daniel and his friends, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah (Rack, Shack and Benny).

But Daniel stays the hand of the man, Arioch the king's captain, by asking him to give Daniel time, and a promise that the Jewish eunuch could find out the kings dream and interpretation.

And in prayer the matter is made known to him by God. And he brings it to Nebuchadnezzar.

That the king dreamed of an idol, a collosal image. Head of gold, chest and two arms of silver, belly and thighs of brass, legs of iron and feet, iron mixed with clay.

And the interpretation thereof,

The Head of Gold: Babylonian Empire

The Chest and Arms of Silver: Medo-Persian Empire

The Belly and Thighs of Brass (Bronze): Greek Empire (Macedonian, under Alexander the Great)

Legs of Iron, the Roman Empire

Feet of Iron and Clay: the Roman Empire divided, and then scattered among the nations.

This is the history that came to pass.

And then we see Jesus. The stone cut from the mountain, without hands. The stone the builders rejected. The foundation upon which is built the everlasting Kingdom. Destroying the kingdoms of men.

**Matthew 21:42**
*Jesus saith unto them, Did ye never read in the scriptures, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner: this is the Lord's doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes?*

*Forasmuch as thou sawest that the stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and that it brake in pieces the iron, the brass, the clay, the silver, and the gold; the great God hath made known to the king what shall come to pass hereafter: and the dream is certain, and the interpretation thereof sure.*

**Mark 12:10**

teachings.title: The Septuagint myth
teachings.summary: Argues the Letter of Aristeas is a forgery, that no Greek Old Testament existed before Christ beyond fragments, that Matthew 5:18 shows Hebrew scripture in use, and that the LXX of Vaticanus and Sinaiticus is a 4th-century revision; answers objections.
teachings.text:
**The Septuagint Myth: Debunking the 2nd Century BC Narrative**

The traditional narrative of the Septuagint (LXX), a supposed 2nd-century BC Greek translation of the Old Testament (OT), is a historical fraud that cannot withstand scrutiny.

The claim—rooted in the pseudepigraphic Letter of Aristeas—that 72 Jewish translators from all 12 tribes, commissioned by Ptolemy II, produced a unified Greek OT is not only implausible but contradicted by manuscript evidence, textual analysis, and biblical context.

As a defender of God’s preserved word in the Hebrew Masoretic Text (MT) and Byzantine Majority Text, I argue that the LXX, as known today in 4th-century AD manuscripts like Codex Vaticanus and Codex Sinaiticus, is a Roman Catholic fabrication, revised to align with New Testament (NT) quotations and shaped by the apostate Catholic Church’s agenda to alter scripture.

Below, I synthesize my case, grounded in the King James Bible (KJV), exposing the LXX myth and its unreliable minority text foundations.

**The Letter of Aristeas: A Forgery**

The Letter of Aristeas, dated to the 2nd century BC, claims Ptolemy II (285–246 BC) commissioned 72 translators—six from each of Israel’s 12 tribes—to translate the Torah into Greek for the Library of Alexandria. This story is a fabrication.

No Egyptian records corroborate Ptolemy’s commission, and the letter’s miraculous account of identical translations reeks of legend, not history.

The involvement of scribes from the 10 northern tribes, dispersed by Assyria in 722 BC (2 Kings 17:6), is anachronistic nonsense, as these tribes were effectively lost. Even non-Levite scribes translating sacred texts stretches credulity, given the Levites’ exclusive role in preserving scripture (Deuteronomy 31:25–26). The Letter is a pseudepigraphic attempt to legitimize Greek texts for Hellenistic Jews, not a historical record.

**Scant Manuscript Evidence**

Manuscript evidence demolishes the idea of a 2nd-century BC Septuagint. Only 1.7–2.6% of the OT survives in Greek from BC sources, per fragments like 4Q120 (Leviticus, 1st century BC) and Papyrus Fouad 266 (Deuteronomy, 2nd–1st century BC). These scraps, covering parts of the Torah and Minor Prophets, are far from a complete OT.

No unified Greek OT manuscript exists from the 1st century AD, when the NT was written. The earliest complete LXX texts—Codex Vaticanus and Codex Sinaiticus—date to the 4th century AD, over 500 years after the supposed translation. These minority texts, riddled with thousands of variants (e.g., 6,000–7,000 NT differences), lack the reliability of the harmonious MT, which aligns closely with the Dead Sea Scrolls (DSS, 250 BC–70 AD).

The DSS, with over 200 Hebrew manuscripts, confirm the MT’s stability, while Greek fragments show textual diversity, suggesting ad hoc translations, not a standardized Septuagint.

**Hebrew Primacy in the NT Era**

The NT assumes a Hebrew textual context, not a Greek one.

In Matthew 5:18 (KJV), Jesus declares, “Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law.” “Jot” (Hebrew yod, smallest letter) and “tittle” (scribal stroke) refer to Hebrew script, meaningless in Greek. This underscores that Hebrew scrolls, not a Greek LXX, were read in 1st-century Judean synagogues (Luke 4:16–20). The DSS, overwhelmingly Hebrew, and rabbinic practices (e.g., Mishnah, Megillah 4:4) confirm Hebrew’s primacy.

While Greek was spoken, NT writers like Paul, fluent in Hebrew, likely translated Hebrew texts into Greek for their audience, not quoted a non-existent Septuagint. Similarities between NT quotations (e.g., Isaiah 7:14, “virgin” in Matthew 1:23) and later LXX texts (e.g., parthenos) result from natural translation of Hebrew terms like almah (virgin or young maiden), not reliance on a unified Greek OT.

**Almah and Translation Integrity**

The claim that NT writers quoted an LXX misreading of almah in Isaiah 7:14 (KJV: “a virgin shall conceive”) is baseless.

Almah, used seven times in the OT (e.g., Genesis 24:43, Rebekah as virgin), denotes a young, unmarried woman, often implying virginity in context (Song of Solomon 6:8). The NT’s parthenos (Matthew 1:23) accurately renders almah’s meaning, reflecting the miraculous sign of a virgin birth. Similarities with 4th-century LXX texts are due to shared translation choices, not NT dependence on a 2nd-century BC Septuagint. Like KJV translators, who used English terms (e.g., “charity” for agape) to convey meaning, NT writers rendered Hebrew into Greek, preserving sense over literalism. This explains overlaps without requiring a mythical LXX.

**4th-Century Revision**

The LXX, as preserved in Vaticanus and Sinaiticus, is a 4th-century AD Roman Catholic product, revised to align with NT quotations. These minority texts, produced in Christian scriptoria, show deliberate harmonization.

For example, Isaiah 7:14’s parthenos in Vaticanus matches Matthew 1:23, supporting the virgin birth, while the MT’s almah is ambiguous. Origen’s Hexapla (240 AD) and the Lucianic recension (300 AD) demonstrate Catholic scribes editing Greek OT texts, often to reflect NT theology.

The Catholic Church, an apostate institution of the 4th century, sponsored this revisionism, as seen in Jerome’s Vulgate (382–405 AD), which included the Apocrypha despite early fathers like Melito and Jerome questioning their canonicity.

The Apocrypha’s inclusion, absent from the Jewish MT and warned against by Athanasius, reflects Catholic tampering, not divine preservation.

**Unreliable Minority Texts**

Vaticanus and Sinaiticus, the backbone of the LXX, are unreliable.

Their 4th-century dating, largely affirmed by Catholic-controlled scholarship (e.g., Vatican Library for Vaticanus), faces providential questions. Sinaiticus’ authenticity is further doubted due to 19th-century forgery claims by Constantine Simonides, who alleged creating it in 1839–1840. While paleography supports their antiquity, their 6,000–7,000 NT variants contrast with the Byzantine Majority Text’s harmony, which underpins the KJV. Westcott and Hort, 19th-century heretics with liberal biases, championed these texts to undermine the Textus Receptus, driven by profit and unorthodox agendas. Their work, like Catholic dating, cannot be trusted against the MT’s fidelity, confirmed by the DSS.

**Objections Answered**

**Objection:** BC Greek fragments (e.g., 4Q120) prove a 2nd-century BC Septuagint.

**Response:** These fragments, covering only 1.7–2.6% of the OT, are disparate, not a unified text. They reflect localized translations, not a Ptolemaic commission.

**Objection:** NT quotations (50–80% LXX-like) suggest a pre-Christian Septuagint.

**Response:** Similarities stem from NT writers translating Hebrew texts, like almah to parthenos. Vaticanus/Sinaiticus were later harmonized to match NT, not quoted in the 1st century.

**Objection:** Jewish use (e.g., Philo) and early papyri show an early LXX.

**Response:** Philo cited individual Greek translations, not a standardized Septuagint. Papyri (e.g., Chester Beatty, 2nd–3rd century AD) are Christian, postdating the NT and reflecting revision, not a 2nd-century BC text.

**Objection:** Catholic scholarship is ecumenical, not controlling dating.

**Response:** The Catholic Church’s history of altering scripture (Vulgate, Apocrypha) and control of Vaticanus taint its credibility. Its apostate status by the 4th century undermines its role as a neutral arbiter.

**Conclusion**

The 2nd-century BC Septuagint is a myth, unsupported by manuscripts, contradicted by Hebrew primacy in the NT (Matthew 5:18), and exposed as a 4th-century AD revision in unreliable minority texts like Vaticanus and Sinaiticus. The Letter of Aristeas is a forgery, BC fragments are negligible, and NT-LXX similarities reflect translation, not a unified Greek OT. The Catholic Church’s apostate influence, from the Vulgate to Apocrypha inclusion, and the dubious scholarship of Westcott and Hort, confirm the LXX’s corruption.

God’s preserved word lies in the MT and the Byzantine Majority Text, faithfully rendered in the KJV. Let us reject the LXX myth and uphold the true scriptures.

teachings.title: Neither... nor in Daniel 11:37
teachings.summary: Walks through the grammar of 'neither... nor' to show that Daniel 11:37 says the antichrist will regard neither the God of his fathers, nor the desire of women, nor any god.
teachings.text:
***Neither shall he regard** the God of his fathers, nor the desire of women...*

For the non-English speaker, understanding basic grammar can be a stumbling block for understanding God's word.

"Neither... nor" is a negative correlative conjunction that connects two or more parts of a sentence to indicate that both options are not true.

"Neither... nor" must be used in parallel structures, meaning both sides must be balanced. For example, if "neither" is followed by a verb, "nor" must also be followed by a verb, or call back to the original verb, and apply it equally to the object of the sentence. For example;

"Neither shall he regard":

"Shall" is the main verb, with "he" as the subject. "Neither" is a coordinating conjunction modifying the verb "shall regard."

"The God of his fathers" is the direct object of "regard."
("The" modifies "God." "Of his fathers" is a prepositional phrase modifying "God.")

"Nor" introduces the second object, "desire" which parallels "God."

("The" modifies "desire."
"Of women" is a prepositional phrase modifying "desire.")

So in the verse about the antichrist, taken from **Daniel 11:37**

*Neither shall he regard the God of his fathers, nor the desire of women, nor regard any god: for he shall magnify himself above all.*

...the Bible says that the antichrist shall not regard the God of his fathers, shall not regard the desire of women, nor shall he regard any god, (small L lords.) Why? For (because, for this reason) he shall magnify himself above all.

It's easy to get caught in strange doctrine and weird beliefs when you don't understand how our language works. Especially when you refuse to attend church and despise correction.

teachings.title: Elisha's bones and the cult of relics
teachings.summary: One verse about Elisha's bones is twisted by Orthodox and Roman churches to justify relic worship, which scripture calls unclean, showing why doctrine must come only from clear scripture compared with scripture.
teachings.text:
Elisha's death occurs in this chapter, and a miracle concerning the prophet; Moabites invade and while burying a man, they spied a band coming, a s so they cast the dead man into the sepulchre of Elisha, and when he was lowered into the tomb, he touched the prophet's bones and revived.

This one short verse is used, primarily by the Orthodox Church, but by many Roman Catholics as well, to justify their veneration and worship of corpses, skulls and bones. Relics, they say, of "holy men," the "saints." They claim the bones have power, that there is Spirit still invested in them, and that this power can be transferred to those that touch them, pray to them, and worship them in rites and rituals.

This pagan cult of relics, worshiping death, serving the dead things of the flesh, is wicked as Hell. As Proverbs says; *all they that hate me love death.*

They store the skeletal remains, usually of unknown origin but with grandiose claims or being Apostles, certain saints, in special places. Temples of death. In glass cases to be paraded about, being served. Miracles are attributed to these abominations. Forgeries abound.

But Scripture gives no such accounting. A miracle occurred. The how and the why aren't given. Elisha isn't exhumed and carted around to temples. No Israelites lined up to seek to be healed by the relics of a finger bone or skull.

No instruction is given by the inspiration of God to do anything of the sort. In fact, we are told repeatedly by the word of God that to do so is unclean. It's gross.

**Numbers 19:13**
*Whosoever toucheth the dead body of any man that is dead, and purifieth not himself, defileth the tabernacle of the LORD; and that soul shall be cut off from Israel*; *because the water of separation was not sprinkled upon him, he shall be unclean; his uncleanness is yet upon him.*

Most of the profane and false doctrines of Rome that have trickled down to the various offshoots of that false church, come from similarly dubious reasoning, where they take a single verse or incident, remove whatever context exists in scripture, and make assumptions and assertions that rely on the foolish reasoning of man, rather than the clear word of God.

This is why we as saved Christians should only take doctrine from clear, undeniable scripture. Proving all things. Comparing spiritual things with spiritual things. Searching the scriptures to see if something is so.

teachings.title: The feasts of the LORD, Passover and the word Easter
teachings.summary: Shows the spring feasts as a picture of Christ's first coming and defends the KJV's use of Easter in Acts 12 against claims that Christian celebration is pagan.
teachings.text:
The Lord God gave Israel Spring feasts and Fall feasts; that served as a picture of Christ.

Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread, now called Easter, the Feast of First Fruits, and the Feast of Weeks also called Pentecost, were given as a picture of Christ's first coming.

The LORD'S feast mirroring the Lord's last supper. The Passover lamb, Christ's sacrifice. The purging of the leaven, the remission of sin. First Fruits, Jesus' resurrection. The Feast of Weeks, Pentecost is known as the Feast of Harvest or the Latter Firstfruits, the day the gospel was preached and 3,000 believed on Christ and took that truth to the ends of the earth, an offering to the Lord.

**1 Corinthians 5:7**
*Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us*.

**1 Corinthians 15:20**
*But now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept.

***Leviticus 23:9-12***
And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye be come into the land which I give unto you, and shall reap the harvest thereof, then ye shall bring a sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest unto the priest: And he shall wave the sheaf before the Lord, to be accepted for you: on the morrow after the sabbath the priest shall wave it. And ye shall offer that day when ye wave the sheaf an he lamb without blemish of the first year for a burnt offering unto the Lord.
*
Similarly, the Fall feasts, or the Harvest feasts; The Feast of Trumpets, the Day of Atonement, and the Feast of Tabernacles, given in **Leviticus 23**, all point to the Day of the Lord, the judgment and the rapture. Jesus' second coming, which throughout the Bible is compared to agricultural terms. Harvests. Bringing in the sheaves. The fruit of believers, after their own kind. The increase going to the Lord.

Amen.

These feasts and days were given of the Lord to us that we may better understand His word, the fulfillment of His promises in the Spring, a time of rebirth, and the prophetic second coming of the end times.

People get caught up in nonsense peddled by some that seek to subvert the faith of many. Vain jangling. And one of the most pernicious is the idea that since pagans had spring and fall feasts, early Christians must have been corrupted by them into adopting them, and so if we mark the occasions in service to the Lord, we are partaking in pagan rituals.

This is wicked as Hell.

Pagans had spring and fall feasts because Satan cannot create, only copy. His pale imitations of the feasts God uses as a parable for His people, were taken from us. Not the other way around.

The Lord Christ Jesus is risen. The final harvest awaits. Let us come rejoicing, bringing in the sheaves.

There is an argument between some KJVOers and those who seek to push false Bible versions and sow doubtful disputations, about the use of the word 'Easter' by the translators in **Acts 12:1-5**;

*Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church. And he killed James the brother of John with the sword. And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also. (Then were the days of unleavened bread.) And when he had apprehended him, he put him in prison, and delivered him to four quaternions of soldiers to keep him; intending after Easter to bring him forth to the people. Peter therefore was kept in prison: but prayer was made without ceasing of the church unto God for him.*

The argument states that since the translators had chosen to use the neologism of William Tyndall, 'Passover' in all other instances where the term 'Pascha' appears in scripture, that either the translation is an error, or they were signifying a completely different feast than Passover.

The transliterated word pascha, from Ancient Greek πάσχα (páskha), from Aramaic פַּסְחָא (paskha), from Hebrew פֶּסַח (pésakh), was used throughout scripture to refer to the Passover feast of the Lord and the feast of Unleavened Bread that follows, commemorating the use of the blood of the lamb, signifying Christ, and the Exodus from Egypt, signifying salvation by the mighty hand of God.

Obviously, those claiming it is a translation error are wrong. The KJV is the inspired and preserved word of God in English. Without error.

But those who should know better claim that the translators made this choice to change what term they used to translate Pascha to teach a secret doctrine of a feast to Astare/Asteroth that Herod was keeping, separate from the Jewish feast.

This is nonsense.

The primary argument is that "Passover is a day. Not the entire week long feast of Unleavened Bread, and it says after Easter, so it can't refer to Passover day! Thus it is a pagan holiday."

This is begging the question. The premises are not true, and so the assumption made isn't an argument.

**Luke 22:1***
Now the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover.*
