Same author as Acts, Luke. Same word being translated, here as Passover, in **Acts 12**, Easter. The Bible defining itself, it refers to the entire feast. All the days.

See also **Deuteronomy 16:1-3**, which refers to Passover and Unleavened Bread as one, long feast;

*Observe the month of Abib, and keep the passover unto the Lord thy God: for in the month of Abib the Lord thy God brought thee forth out of Egypt by night. Thou shalt therefore sacrifice the passover unto the Lord thy God, of the flock and the herd, in the place which the Lord shall choose to place his name there. Thou shalt eat no leavened bread with it; seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread therewith, even the bread of affliction; for thou camest forth out of the land of Egypt in haste: that thou mayest remember the day when thou camest forth out of the land of Egypt all the days of thy life.*

So we know that these were the *days* of unleavened bread, that Herod sought to please the Jews, and so he arrested Peter, intending to bring him forth to the people, to be executed like James had been, after Pascha had ended. After the feast of Unleavened Bread. After Passover. After Easter.

There is no other argument made in this regard that comes from scripture. And there is no argument put forth using scripture that supports the claim that this refers to a pagan feast, rather than the Pascha of the Lord.

That the translators used the only chronological mention of Passover, the feast of Unleavened Bread, that appears in scripture, following the resurrection, to refer to the feast using the English term Christians called it, differentiating the OT understanding from the NT, is in my opinion a deliberate choice. Again, the Bible defining itself.

And the final nail in the coffin of this weird doctrine, that the translators were not talking about the Passover feast, from the feast of the Lord through resurrection Sunday, which takes place during the days of Unleavened Bread, but were actually cluing us in to Herod being a pagan celebrating a feast to Asteroth, is that they included this handy chart to track the days given the difference between the Gregorian calendar and the shifting lunar calendar used by the Hebrews to mark the days.

"To find Easter for ever." They were not including a means to find the date of a pagan festival. They knew what the word meant to Christians for hundreds of years before them. Easter being used by the earlier translators in place of Pascha, who didn't rely on Tyndall's newly invented 'Passover.'

It is preposterous to claim to be KJVO and then say the translators included a pagan holiday calendar in it.

They did not make an error and they did not mean a feast for Astare.

They meant the Pascha, and the risen Christ.

"But there are pagan spring holidays that have rabbits and eggs and fertility ceremonies and sacrifices! Modern use of a bunny and baskets with chocolate eggs are pagan, so the entire thing must be rejected!"

Again, pagans do a lot of things that they copied from God. The first animal sacrifice is God teaching Adam and Eve about Jesus. Pagans do animal sacrifices too. I guess God was teaching them to be pagans.

Just because localized cultural traditions spring up (no pun intended) around Christian holy days, doesn't make the holy day wrong.

When a pastor or someone claiming to be a teacher brings forth a strange doctrine that cannot be proven from scripture, but relies on a fallacious argument, extra biblical sources and teaching for commandments the doctrines of men, judging those who disagree or trying to sow doubtful disputations with those weak in the faith, search the scriptures to see if it is so. The Bible is the final authority.

**Colossians 2:16-17**
*Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.*

One more thing; invariably, almost without fail, the people who push these internet doctrines the hardest, that seek to make celebration of Christ's birth, death and resurrection into pagan festivals to discourage Christians from celebrating, are hardcore Judaizers.

Lots of sincere Bible-believing, soul winning, separated Christians get caught up in these things, and are just trying to do the right thing for the Lord, as their conscience sees it. **This is not about them**. I want to make that very very clear.

But the ones who seem to push the notion that "Celebrating traditional Christian holidays is actually pagan. So don't do it!" the most are Hebrew roots types. Like the one who just spammed my chat with some nonsense meme using "hashem" and other Jewish terms to say if you celebrate Easter you aren't saved.

Jews main argument against Christianity is that it is a pagan religion. They push their noahide law doctrines on Gentiles, that flat out states worshiping of Christ is Idolatry, punishable by death. By beheading.

And to that end, they promote things like the pagan origins of holy days, and push Christians to adopt Hebrew feasts. To keep the Sabbath. To blow the shofar.

It is no wonder that churches heavily influenced by dispensationalism, Zionism, and the pre-tribulation rapture, also often fall prey to these memes. They will also teach things like the Satan seed heresy, that nephilim are half breeds, and that "God is not done with Israel yet."

I think dispensationalism is a foot in the door for Judaizers. And Jewish fables claiming that Christianity is just Mithraism, that Enoch is hidden scripture, or that Easter is a pagan holiday, are deliberately done to make the name of Christ be hid. To bring us under bondage. As a snare.

That false churches like the Roman Catholics do pagan things in their religion gives these Judaizers ammunition. They feed each other and do the work of Satan.

teachings.title: Alive without the law once
teachings.summary: He shows original sin relies on corrupt versions like the NIV and leads to infant baptism and limbo, while Romans 7:9 shows we die spiritually when we knowingly sin.
teachings.text:
I will note too that in order to wrest **Psalm 51:5** to say that babies are born sinning and carrying sin generationally, they use corrupt versions of the Bible like the NIV;

Surely I was sinful at birth, sinful from the time my mother conceived me.

Just like most other heresies, they need to twist and rend meaning that's not there to create proof texts.

And like most other heresies, they then need to build on their error to make it fit with other verses that clearly contradict their interpretation.

Sinning from birth, where a baby has no understanding of right and wrong, no sinful needs, only to eat, sleep and grow, no need to covet, is an absurdity. But if you accept this absurd doctrine, then you have to deal with the untimely deaths of infants. Miscarriages and still births. Young toddlers dying in their cribs.

If they are born sinning, and carrying the guilt of sin their parents committed, then those babies by necessity are damned.

And if infants without the law or understanding of right from wrong are sent to Hell for eternity, then that cruelty would offend people, especially mothers.

So, to square this seeming injustice with a perfectly just God, the invention of baby baptism, "Limbo," the extension of grace from Christ's sacrifice for sin extended to children to some arbitrary "age of accountability," and other strange doctrines were formed. Even going so far as to extend Calvinistic predestination to the infants, so that either some babies are elect, and others damned (James White), or by God's grace and mercy, all children who die young also happen to be elect (Reformers who know how evil White sounds).

The simple answer is found in **Romans 7:9**

*For I was alive without the law once: but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died.*

The simple understanding that, at some point innocence ends, at the understanding of the law, knowing right from wrong, and we choose sin. And when we do, our spirit dies.

God is just. We must choose salvation in Christ, because we all inevitably choose sin. But those who have no capacity for either choice are not slain in the spirit, or in need of having it quickened again.

Infants are in the same state as Adam in the garden, before breaking the one commandment of God. Their needs cared for by others. Incapable of sin until they can willingly transgress the law of God. And afterwards, like Adam. They fall, and learn the knowledge of good and evil. They die to sin, spiritually.

There is no hard and fast rule of what age this happens. There are some who as soon as they gain understanding, choose evil. This could be as young as a toddler. It could be as a tween. It may be that a developmentally delayed or retarded person never fully gains this understanding, while others do and get saved or become wicked.

teachings.title: It is always a choice
teachings.summary: Israel chose of their own free will to leave the work undone, and God gave His word as testimony so men would believe, using even their disobedience for His purpose.
teachings.text:
Just to recap the theme going into the **Book of Judges**; God having delivered the people into the promised land commanded them to utterly destroy the inhabitants and to smash down their altars to the false gods they worshipped. The Lord had been with them in every battle (save one, thanks to the abomination of Achan). He had driven out the people that Joshua and his armies went against. He delivered 33 Kings into their hands. The Lord God rained hail the size of boulders, drove men out with hornets, felled the walls of cities with the shout and trumpets of the Israelites.

But yet they did not fully eradicate the Canaanites and others in the land. They resorted to allowing them to stay in tribute. Valuing their gold more than the commandments of God.

They had the knowledge of the will of the sovereign God, and *chose*, of their own will, to ignore His word, to do as they saw was right in their own eyes. Despite all their valiant deeds and the miracles they witnessed while obeying Him, they slacked off in their duty to do that which was comfortable. Easy. To leave the work unfinished.

By their choice. By free will.

And God responded by removing the hedge of protection around them. By allowing them to feel the consequences of their actions. By using these nations as a thorn in the side of Israel, to prove her that they may learn the ways of war, rather than peace. To be a snare with their false gods, so that the glory of God could be known. That in their tribulation they would call out to the Lord for salvation, and He would place His Spirit on a judge He would raise up to deliver them.

The Bible is the record of God's will for man, in Christ Jesus. And it demonstrates that He gave His word as a testimony, that man should believe Him. The Godhead being three persons, that the witness be true, just as the law requires. Jesus appeared resurrected to witnesses that others believed their report. The Spirit indwells believers, that it testify to them they have eternal life, that they may **know**. The Bible exists, inspired and preserved, that we may hear the word and have faith that it is true, and obey His commandments beginning with the gospel of Christ.

It is always a choice. And God uses our choices to His purpose, even when we are disobedient. Even when some don't believe the report. Even when people fall away from the truth.

teachings.title: A copy of the law for kings and heirs
teachings.summary: As kings were to copy and read the law, believers who will reign with Christ must learn scripture to judge rightly, turning neither to the political left nor right but to God's way.
teachings.text:
*And it shall be, when he sitteth upon the throne of his kingdom, that he shall write him a copy of this law in a book out of that which is before the priests the Levites: And it shall be with him, and he shall read therein all the days of his life: that he may learn to fear the Lord his God, to keep all the words of this law and these statutes, to do them: That his heart be not lifted up above his brethren, and that he turn not aside from the commandment, to the right hand, or to the left: to the end that he may prolong his days in his kingdom, he, and his children, in the midst of Israel.*

This command for kings, for those that rule over others in judgement, holds the most application for us today out of the other warnings for future kings.

We who are saved are heirs to the Kingdom. Admonishments and advice given throughout the OT, and New, are given that we may know right judgment. Not only in this life, but in the Millennial Kingdom, where we are to rule and reign with Christ.

This is an often overlooked aspect of our Christian life. We will judge angels. We are called to be part of the hierarchy of God's divine plan. As husbands, wives, parents, children, servants. As men over thousands, hundreds and tens. To judge the fatherless and advocate for the widow. And as princes of His Kingdom.

And the administration of His Kingdom requires men and women of understanding. This is the most important thing about Bible study, learning scripture and committing the word of God to our hearts. That we may know His will and execute His judgements with mercy, grace and longsuffering. With understanding.

God told whomever would be king of Israel to make a handwritten copy of the law, that they may know it. That he may keep the statutes and in doing so, serve with a humble heart. This applies to us so much today, and it is as neglected as Solomon neglected it in his day.

God's promise is that we will prolong our days on this earth, that would be well with us and with those who he is given us authority over. And authority under.

When we know his commandments and try to keep them, and we understand his judgment and try to see things the way God does, We will turn neither to the left hand nor the right.

We've been trained all our lives to use the left and the right as shorthand for two diametrically opposed philosophies. But the truth is we as Christians are supposed to embrace a third way; God's way. What is right in His eyes rather than our own.

Many of us identify with the so-called right? Because they are correct in many of their assessments of what's wrong and seem to be moving towards a godly return to tradition. But that can only carry us so far. In the end we are not to turn either to the left or the right, but to maintain the straight paths He has set before us. We would do well to remember that as princess of the Kingdom. Sons of the King.

teachings.title: Tongues are for a sign to unbelievers
teachings.summary: Tongues were a sign to unbelievers that they might hear the gospel, showing God's word keeps its power in every language, and gifts are to be used decently with charity.
teachings.text:
**1 Corinthians 14:18-22**
 *I thank my God, I speak with tongues more than ye all: Yet in the church I had rather speak five words with my understanding, that by my voice I might teach others also, than ten thousand words in an unknown tongue.*

*Brethren, be not children in understanding: howbeit in malice be ye children, but in understanding be men. In the law it is written, With men of other tongues and other lips will I speak unto this people; and yet for all that will they not hear me, saith the Lord. Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to them that believe, but to them that believe not: but prophesying serveth not for them that believe not, but for them which believe*

Just to reinforce this point; that the purpose of the 1st century churches having members who could speak or understand foreign languages was to be as a sign for the unsaved, that they may hear the Gospel and believe, knowing the power of God.

This means that God's word can be translated into all languages and remain powerful and give faith and keep the same meaning. Even if phrased in the manner and custom of the language itself.

All languages are of God. From Babel to today.

The gift of speaking to others that they may be saved hasn't gone away. It just requires some effort. But the same Spirit works in us, that if we begin a good thing for the work of Christ, He is faithful to help us achieve it.

*If any man think himself to be a prophet, or spiritual, let him acknowledge that the things that I write unto you are the commandments of the Lord.*

In other words, if some claim to be better than, more spiritual than others, more "gifted" then this epistle should set them right that they aren't. That these gifts and whatever talent we have been blessed with by God are to be used in an orderly and decent manner, with charity towards all.

teachings.title: The gifts of wisdom and knowledge
teachings.summary: The manifestation of the Spirit is given to profit others, and wisdom and knowledge come by studying the word to serve the brethren, not to be puffed up.
teachings.text:
*But the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal.*

The things of the Spirit are for others' profit. But if they are used as a sign of salvation, or holiness, as an indicator of individual righteousness and worse, prominence in the assembly, they aren't of any benefit at all, except to those who seek to be seen as better-than. Holier than thou.

Paul gives examples of the gifts of the Spirit. Note these may be supernatural but aren't superpowers. This isn't a comic book. While some may be miraculous, they are by God, to His purpose. But most are simply talents as are divided among men *severally*, or individually; each in turn.

**Wisdom and knowledge**, which we know are from the Spirit for all men, that the knowledge of how the world is and the understanding of what that knowledge means is a revelation of God. Even among the unsaved and profane, and true wisdom of this world comes from God, and His word, inspired, taught and reproved by the Spirit, through the righteous in Christ.

Even when a depraved and reprobate person like Jordan Peterson or Deepak Chopra expresses some kernel of truth within their nonsense philosophies of men, it is from God and His word and the recognition of that truth in men is by revelation of Him through the Spirit, reproving the world.

That we who are of Christ and partakers of the gift of eternal life, are able to study the word of God, and to know His will through scripture, receiving the spiritual things of God, we are given knowledge and wisdom. Walking in the Spirit, we are given that gift, that the natural man receiveth not.

That is why Peter and John, uneducated and common men, were able to speak with such excellency of knowledge and wisdom: **Acts 4:13**

*Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled; and they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.*

As Christ promised, the Comforter brings to remembrance all that He spoke, and understanding of all that the prophets gave witness to.

This is a gift that we can all enjoy, by walking in the Spirit. By studying to be approved. By humbling ourselves to know nothing but Christ, and Him crucified. Comparing spiritual things with spiritual. Scripture with scripture. Letting God tell us His will; **Hebrews 4:12**

*For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.*

But that knowledge and wisdom is not to put ourselves above other brethren, but to humbly serve them that they may grow in the same. **2 Timothy 2:15**;

*Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.*

Approved unto God. Not justified among men. Not to be pridefully arrogant in knowledge, (and showing a lack of wisdom) by applying the wisdom of men to the things of God, as so many do.

Internet theologians, special boys well versed in the vain philosophy and traditions of men, who through much learning of those rudiments of "muh church fathers" and "the reformers," or worse, doctrines of devils drawn from their own invention, ever learning but never come to the actual knowledge of the Truth.
Remembering that, *being many, are one body in Christ, and every one members one of another.* And remembering that our purpose is to profit others.

teachings.title: The things of God are spiritually discerned
teachings.summary: Understanding of the things of God is a gift of the Spirit through the word, so the natural man who seeks worldly wisdom finds them foolishness.
teachings.text:
Continuing this study on Spiritual Gifts, here in **1 Corinthians 2**. Paul is writing to the church at Corinth to address divisions there, the first being those disputing about who is better among them by the minister of the gospel they'd received it by.

Paul, who along with Apollos and Peter, is being touted by some as greater, and so he humbly seeks to set the record straight. That he didn't preach to them with excellency of words and speech, an orator, or with particular wisdom and logic, as the Greeks taught in their vain philosophy. He declared the testimony of God win meekness and in fear, and in much trembling. Bringing to them the knowledge of Christ crucified, a demonstration to them of the Spirit, and the power of God.

The wisdom of the world is brought to nothing by the wisdom of God. But that wisdom is only revealed, can only be known, by His Spirit.

This is a gift of the Spirit, that all are called and those that believe bear witness to the power of God and by the understanding of His word through the Holy Ghost.

The things of God are unknown to man, but by the Spirit of God.

*Now we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the spirit which is of God; that we might know the things that are freely given to us of God*.

This is important. Without first believing the Gospel, preached by the power of the word of God, and the understanding by the Spirit, the things of God are foolishness to man.

The Holy Ghost teaches, not the wisdom of men, not of the world, but the spiritual things of God. Comparing spiritual things with spiritual.

*But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.*

The knowledge and understanding of the things of God is a gift of the Holy Ghost. The Spirit of God gives us understanding, from His word.

This is why so many who deny the simple Gospel, and chase after the wisdom of men, who seek knowledge of the world rather than the spiritual things of God, say such foolish things regarding God, salvation, doctrine and scripture. They cannot understand because these things are spiritually discerned. They are given us of the Spirit through the word.

teachings.title: Spiritual blindness and willingness to receive
teachings.summary: Heretics who seek validation rather than truth are spiritually blind, while saved people misled can be corrected by scripture if willing.
teachings.text:
This gift of the Spirit, understanding of the things of God. Even the deep things, the meat of the word, comes from studying scripture, to be approved by God. As we seek, so to He gives wisdom and understanding freely, through the Spirit within us.

We often run into people, especially now online, who are lost in heresy. Who have, what seems to us, foolish understanding of basic doctrines, that we try to correct from clear scripture, and they cannot see it. They are spiritually blind. They trust the wisdom of other men and their own logic, given of the world, to try and figure out what are the spiritual things of God. Because they don't seek the truth, but validation for their own ideas, they cannot receive that gift of understanding the Spirit provides.

This can even strike the saved, misled by itching ears to hear false doctrine given by theologians and tradition, and every other thing but comparing spiritual things to spiritual. They may be led to understanding by being reproached with scripture. They aren't completely blind. But they still have to be willing to receive it.

Paul, inspired by the Spirit and preaching the word of God by letter, to be read to the Corinthians, is doing exactly this; Showing those willing to be given understanding, the wisdom of God.

*For who hath known the mind of the Lord, that he may instruct him? but we have the mind of Christ*.

teachings.title: Dispensationalism falls apart by comparing scripture
teachings.summary: Dispensationalism survives only on proof texts stripped of context, and falls apart when scripture is compared with scripture.
teachings.text:
Anyone who tries to justify Dispensationalism to defend their Zionist fever dreams and heretical end times doctrine has to rely on making each argument in a vacuum. Stripping proof texts from their surrounding meaning. By ignoring contradictions and clear verses, to make doctrine from non sequiturs.

But when we compare scripture to scripture, their doctrines fall apart.

That is why they will make sweeping proclamations and assertions and arguments that are only backed by the stripped-away proof text, and not by the whole context of Scripture.

It is why their false teachers will discourage reading the Bible yourself. Studying to be approved before God. They will over complicate it, make you doubt the word. Use false translations, study guides and charts. Tell you you have to "God back to the Greek!" or Hebrew. Imply that if you don't understand it the way they present it, you must not be saved.

And inevitably, they will use Judaizing to bring a false gospel of works to reinforce their own wicked doctrines.

Dispensationalism has crept in to good, KJV, Bible believing churches with the right Gospel, no doubt. And many saved Christians are misled by it.

But if you look at how far along the spectrum of Dispensationalism they are, the more damnable heresy creeps in.

A little leaven leavens the whole lump.

teachings.title: Dispensationalism in light of Romans
teachings.summary: Romans 1 lays the foundation against reading Romans 11:26 as Zionism: the gospel of Christ was promised by all the prophets and the dispensation of grace has been in effect from the beginning.
teachings.text:
**Dispensationalism in light of the Book of Romans.**

The events of the past week have seen an increase in the false claim that modern Jews occupying the Levant are the Israel of God, not saved believers. To defend this heretical garbage, those supporting this claim will use a handful of scripture, but they especially rely on **Romans 11:26**;

*And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob*

Stripped of context, this appears to support their false teaching, but luckily for us, we have the entirety of Romans to demonstrate why this interpretation is wrong, and frankly dishonest.

For the next few days I am going to go over the building blocks for the arguments made by Paul in Romans to refute that reading of 11:26, once and for all. Starting today in **Romans 1**;

*Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God, (Which he had promised afore by his prophets in the holy scriptures,) Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh; And declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead: By whom we have received grace and apostleship, for obedience to the faith among all nations, for his name: Among whom are ye also the called of Jesus Christ*

In **Romans**, the often abused epistle to the believers in Rome, Paul makes several arguments, and in the Spirit, these arguments build upon each other, each underpinning the next.

Here in the opening greeting, Paul stipulated several important and fundamental points as a foundation of everything that follows.

Paul is a servant of Jesus Christ, separated unto the Gospel of God. This is important. It isn't separation from; it isn't separation from the world, from sin, from his previous beliefs prior to salvation. It is towards something, with a purpose. And that something is not only the Gospel of Jesus in the sense we generally think of, the 4 books that tells us His life, teachings, death and resurrection, but Paul places the entire canon of scripture up to that point, the Old Testament as we refer to it, as the good news of God, because to Him all prophets gave witness.

As Christ says;

**John 5:46-47**
*For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me. But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?*

This is important to establish. Jesus being the fulfilment of the prophets and the oracles of God sets the context for everything that follows. Paul is going to give the final word on the Dispensation of Grace, and how it relates to both Jew and Gentiles. And this dispensation has been in effect from the beginning. It is of God, given in sundry times and diverse places to the fathers by the prophets, moved by the Spirit.

The only new revelation is that it is Jesus who is called upon, the mystery of salvation that always existed, revealed in these last times, that all who call upon the name of the Lord are saved.

The promise of God in Christ, His good news that He's been telling the patriarchs and the Hebrews in general, from the beginning, that Jews always had access to. They *should* know and have recognized who Jesus was.

Paul then gives a concise rendition of that Gospel by which he and the Romans he is writing to (and we today), know we are saved:

-Jesus was **made flesh** through the seed of David
-Declared **the Son of God** with power. Many signs miracles and wonders. Raising the dead and healing the sick. Preaching the word with authority, etc, **According to the Spirit of Holiness**
-And **by the resurrection from the dead**
-**By whom we received grace**, apostleship, **called of Jesus Christ**.

God became flesh and dwelt among us, was killed and raised from the dead as God promised, and all who answered the call are given the grace of God, the gift of eternal life. Called to follow Him and spread this good news to all nations.

teachings.title: Metanoia: repentance is a change of mind toward God
teachings.summary: Explains the word translated repentance as a change of mind and heart toward God and belief, and argues that adding "of sin" came with modern versions.
teachings.text:
*Metanoia*, the Greek word translated in our King James Bible as "repentance," is a changing of the mind. “Meta” comes from the root for “after” or “beyond,” while “noeo” is “to think.” So metanoeo means to reconsider or to rethink something. At its root, repentance is about changing one's mind. 'Metanoia' literally means to 'change your mind, to change direction' …has nothing to do with guilt or shame.

So, when John the Baptist calls his audience to repent, he is telling them to understand the Kingdom is at hand and to have a thorough change of heart and mind regarding salvation and the coming Christ. To reconsider and believe. To be convicted in the Spirit. To turn towards God.

This has always been its meaning and no one changed it until modern Bible versions in the 20th century began to append "..of sin" and delete the instances of God's repentance, to begin pushing the Devil's favorite damnable heresy, works salvation.

That's why in scripture, again and again, repentance and belief are used in tandem to express conversion, by believing on Jesus and receiving the gift of eternal life promised by God.

This is the Gospel of the Bible and how men have been saved from the time of Seth. The notion that it was changed or twisted in the 1980s to something other than that is not only biblically and linguistically wrong, it is absurd.

" In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea, And saying, Feel bad about sinning and try not to sin: for the kingdom of Heaven is at hand."

Hey that sounds like works...

teachings.title: Give the gospel from scripture, not rhetoric
teachings.summary: Faith comes by hearing the word, so a true gospel presentation leads through scripture, while false prophets paraphrase to avoid being pinned down.
teachings.text:
Now [here](https://youtu.be/F8owXQ2QyvA) is the Gospel presentation that I took that screenshot from. Notice that the Pastor uses scripture to lead the listener through the Gospel.

The Bible says that faith comes by hearing the word of God. The power is in the word. God uses scripture to prick our hearts.

You see Philip with the eunuch expounds on who Christ is from scripture, guiding him. When Paul and Silas were with the Philippian jailer, who asks "What must I do to be saved," they say believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, *And they spake unto him the word of the Lord, and to all that were in his house.*

Oftentimes, when you see a false prophet attempting to give their version of what it takes to be saved (if they can be pinned down to do so) they don't use scripture, but rather their own paraphrasing rhetoric.

The scriptures are a rock. They do not change. But by avoiding direct reference to the Bible, they are able to avoid being pinned down, and can twist or add to Biblical concepts, such as appending "...of your sins" to every appearance of "repent."

**Romans 10:11-17**
*For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed. For there is no difference between the Jew and the Greek: for the same Lord over all is rich unto all that call upon him. For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things! But they have not all obeyed the gospel. For Esaias saith, Lord, who hath believed our report?*

*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*

teachings.title: Nadab and Abihu offered strange fire
teachings.summary: Nadab and Abihu died for adding their own works to God's commanded worship, the same error as those who follow traditions and church fathers over scripture.
teachings.text:
Over the course of 9 chapters we have seen the detailed instructions from the Lord to Moses, telling the Levitical priesthood of Aaron and his eldest two sons with great specificity, what they were to do regarding purification and sacrifice, where and how and when, and to what portion was God's, the blood, the burnt offering, the wave and the heave offerings, all of it.

And despite these clear and explicit teachings of the word of God, the first thing the newly anointed sons of Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, do is add their own works to it.

They light incense with a "strange fire," that is not the fire the Lord provided within the Tabernacle, but fire they made themselves. Their intentions seem to be good; they offered this strange fire before the Lord. They were seeking to praise Him, perhaps. Glorifying God with their own invention of religious expression, which the Lord commanded them not.

*And there went out fire from the Lord, and devoured them, and they died before the Lord.*

Aaron, chosen to be the first high priest of the Levitical priesthood, honored by his sons being chosen with him, to lead the congregation and perform the propitiations and oblations, to instruct the people in the ways of salvation through Christ by their adherence to the commands of God, in sanctification, showing the judgment of God that all the people may glorify Him. And he watches his sons burn to death, seeking their own righteousness.

The error of Cain is a natural impulse for man. To add our own works or to place new and strange ways of worship upon the things of God that His word instructs, is something we see throughout the Bible. And we see God's judgement upon those who seek their own sanctification, their own means of being holy. Who add to His word. Who brings their own works to the table of the Lord.

And yet, it continues.

Just as Judaizers and those teaching strange doctrines of men were creeping in unawares to the early New Testament churches. Just as heretics and apostates twisted the word of God, bringing another gospel, so too did *Nadab and Abihu*.

Those who claim that the "church fathers" were correct when they deviated from scripture and that there were hidden traditions, passed down from apostles, are the same as those who Jude wrote about in his epistle;

*Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core.*

They bring strange fire before the Lord.

teachings.title: Faith cometh by hearing the word
teachings.summary: Winning souls is the work of eternal value, and the power to save is in the preached word of God, not our arguments or tracts.
teachings.text:
Our entire purpose as vessels fit for righteousness, is spreading and sending others to spread the word of God, that He may have the increase. That the harvest, which is plentiful have laborers to bring in the sheaves. That we be servants of the Gospel. Ministers of His word.

**1 Corinthians 3:5-8**
*Who then is Paul, and who is Apollos, but ministers by whom ye believed, even as the Lord gave to every man? I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase. So then neither is he that planteth any thing, neither he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase. Now he that planteth and he that watereth are one: and every man shall receive his own reward according to his own labour.*

These are the works that matter. That have eternal value. That, unlike the wood, hay and stubble of our own vain works and filthy rags of our own righteousness which burn up, the winning of souls and edification of others that they may win souls are the precious stones, silver and gold that remain. The eternal value of those things we build up on the foundation that is Christ.

We must be sent, into the highways and hedges, preaching the Gospel to every creature, so that they may hear the word of God, and by hearing, believe, and by their faith, confess the truth with their mouths, that they too may be sent. This is the way.

Note the power is in the word we preach. The word of God found in scripture.

*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*

The power to save men's souls is in God's word. Not our logical arguments, not in our boasts or testimonials. Certainly not in our selfish acts of following the letter of the law, the vain traditions of men, washing the outside of the cup while the inside is filthy. But by scripture.

*Faith cometh by hearing and hearing by the word of God*, preached by those that believe, sent to gather for the harvest.

*For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.*

This is an important idea for saved Christians to grasp. That for all the efforts made to send people tracts, pocket New Testaments, door hangers and invitations to church, and our own attempts to get people to believe by our rephrasing and paraphrasing and using logic, none of it saves.

*Faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*

The power is in the word. The Spirit works through the word, given by believers to bring men to faith. And so we should not hide that light under a bushel. We should shout it from the rooftops.

*For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth*.

teachings.title: There is one gospel
teachings.summary: Galatians was written against Judaizers who demanded the law and slandered Paul, and the same attacks on Paul recur today, but anyone bringing another gospel is accursed.
teachings.text:
Everyone should really read this introduction to the Epistle to the various churches throughout Galatia.

Paul is writing to churches he founded on the gospel, the only good news that we are forgiven all sin and given eternal life through the life, death and resurrection of Jesus Christ, the Son of God. He is writing them because Jews have come behind him, telling the Gentile believers they must follow the law and be circumcised to be saved. Trying to drag who they can back to bondage. To judaize the churches, and to damn the people who had believed in vain, never really trusting in Christ alone.

And these judaizers had badmouthed Paul, claiming he wasn't a real Apostle, that he preached a different Gospel than Peter and even than Jesus Christ.

Sound familiar?

(It's a trend in our circles and on pol, for example, that comes around like clockwork every few months. There are patterns to heresy. They come in waves.)

Discrediting Paul, who God chose to give the authoritative theology for people saved by faith, Jew or Greek, to write the afterwards and lay out everything that came before it and the implications for a Christian life, just as James, Jude, Peter and John.

For there is one gospel and anyone bringing another is accursed.

And the Apostles agreed with Paul when he went to them in Acts about this very thing, which prompted those other epistles and more like them not in scripture.

teachings.title: He led captivity captive
teachings.summary: Ephesians 4 says Christ rose with the keys of death and Hell and so led captivity captive, and gives no hint of freeing saints from a holding room in Hell.
teachings.text:
**Ephesians 4**
*4 There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling;*

*5 One Lord, one faith, one baptism,*

*6 One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.*

*7 But unto every one of us is given grace according to the measure of the gift of Christ.*

*8 Wherefore he saith, When he ascended up on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts unto men.*

*9 (Now that he ascended, what is it but that he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth?*

*10 He that descended is the same also that ascended up far above all heavens, that he might fill all things.)*

The letter to the Ephesians, Paul is writing regarding spiritual gifts and the like, and references **Psalm 68**, regarding the gifts given to men by God. Quoting verse 18, which says God ascended up on high, leading captivity captive, Paul takes the time to parenthetically mention that Jesus, who conquered Hell and Death when He was risen from Hell, had first descended. Note the order of things. The line about captivity captive isn't part of that parenthetical point.

It doesn't say Jesus freed saints from some holding room in Hell. It doesn't even hint at it.

We are all captives of sin, and the wages of sin are death. But by rising from the dead with the keys to death and Hell, Jesus led captivity captive. Amen.

**Revelation 1:18**
*I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death.*

teachings.title: Faith comes by hearing the Gospel, not by appeals to the world
teachings.summary: Responds to a worldly outreach campaign by showing that faith comes by hearing the word of God, and warns against being embarrassed by the Gospel or trying to win sinners by appeals to emotion or reason.
teachings.text:
I guess the #HeGetsUs campaign is the Hobby Lobby CEO's pet project, and at least going by his church's statement of faith, he believes in Biblical salvation.

Maybe he sincerely believes that he can reach people about Jesus without actually using the Gospel. Seems like a fools errand.

*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*..

There's a certain embarrassment about that concept, and sharing the Gospel in general that many saved Christians have. They think they have to appeal to the sensual, the fleshly and worldly in order to get sinners to consider Jesus "at least as a great teacher with good things we should all listen to," rather than by the Spirit, using the word of God which has the power to save.

It may come from a sincere person who doesn't quite get that faith isn't found in an appeal to logic, reason or emotion. It comes from hearing the word.

It often comes from culturally imbued embarrassment, of wanting to be liked by others and seeing use of the Bible to give people the good news as being "preachy" and "judgey." Not wanting to "scare off people," but really it's just the vanity of wanting worldly people to respect them and their opinion, rather than sharing their faith.

Some evangelicals believe they have to trick people into hearing about Jesus. That if they do flashy ad campaigns about Jesus the man, the viewers might absorb things about Jesus the Christ and Son of God, by osmosis.

This is the same impulse that drives turning churches into a Panic at the Disco concert led by effeminate men in skinny jeans only preaching love, and not against sin or from scripture. Thinking if they use fog machines and lasers and uplifting pop music, and not preach hard against sin, they won't alienate people and maybe one might actually get saved.

But we aren't saved by the flesh.

*Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? Are ye so foolish? having begun in the Spirit, are ye now made perfect by the flesh? Have ye suffered so many things in vain? if it be yet in vain.*

The Holy Spirit has a ministry to the unsaved.

*Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you. And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment: Of sin, because they believe not on me; Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more; Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged.*

For unregenerate man is called by the Spirit, led by the Spirit and convicted by the Spirit, and the word of God is spirit and life.

*It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.*

And so, looking through the materials of the #HeGetsUs campaign, that doesn't have a single appeal from scripture to salvation, it really looks more like a vain attempt to make Christians seem cool, rather than proclaim the truth that saved them.

But, the Bible says we shouldn't be ashamed of the Gospel. It is the power of God.

*For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth.*

And as we know, faith comes from hearing the word of God.

*How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things! But they have not all obeyed the gospel. For Esaias saith, Lord, who hath believed our report?*

Don't be ashamed to give the gospel from scripture, unapologetically and unashamedly. It is in the word that God's power lay. Not in our anecdotes or testimonials. Not in appeals to the "red letters" on "how to live." But in the surety of the Spirit testifying within us, given by God through His word.

*For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.*

teachings.title: Faith expected to grow
teachings.summary: After salvation our faith should grow by believing a preserved Bible and its doctrine, avoiding the snares of false teachers and carnal readings of scripture.
teachings.text:
Once you believe on the gospel and have faith that it's true, that Jesus died for your sins and that you have eternal life that can never be lost or taken away from you because of His perfect work on the cross, your faith is expected to grow.

We are conformed into the vessel that God needs for His purpose. In order to do that, you have to believe that you can find the will of God. You have to have faith that His word is available to us that we may know His will. You have to have a Bible that contains the whole word that you believe is inspired and preserved. You have to believe the doctrine that His will reveals to us through the Holy Spirit. You have to have faith that it's not by your works of righteousness but by those He has elected us too do. By His will not ours.

There are many stumbling blocks and snares laid in our path as we run towards the finish that we are predestinated for. They are laid there by people who either are not saved and fumbling, or are vipers who are deliberately misleading. You miss out on so much of God's word and the joy of living faith to faith. Contending for the faith set before us.

We've all been sidetracked off of the path by doctrines of devils and doubtful disputations at one point or another. Getting caught up in the worldly aspects that people draw out of scripture, taking things in a carnal way like Nicodemus.

In that we lose track of the spiritual aspects. Which, when we have faith in them, transforms us here in this world that we may better serve him and His will, for His glory in the next.

teachings.title: What 'led captivity captive' means
teachings.summary: Shows from Judges 5 that leading captivity captive means taking one's captors captive, and applies it to Christ rising from three days in Hell with victory over death and Hell, not freeing captives from Hell.
teachings.text:
**Judges 5:12-13**
*Awake, awake, Deborah: awake, awake, utter a song: arise, Barak, and lead thy captivity captive, thou son of Abinoam. Then he made him that remaineth have dominion over the nobles among the people: the Lord made me have dominion over the mighty.*

**Psalm 68:12-19**
*Kings of armies did flee apace: and she that tarried at home divided the spoil. Though ye have lien among the pots, yet shall ye be as the wings of a dove covered with silver, and her feathers with yellow gold. When the Almighty scattered kings in it, it was white as snow in Salmon.

The hill of God is as the hill of Bashan; an high hill as the hill of Bashan. Why leap ye, ye high hills? this is the hill which God desireth to dwell in; yea, the Lord will dwell in it for ever. The chariots of God are twenty thousand, even thousands of angels: the Lord is among them, as in Sinai, in the holy place.

Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive: thou hast received gifts for men; yea, for the rebellious also, that the Lord God might dwell among them. Blessed be the Lord, who daily loadeth us with benefits, even the God of our salvation. Selah.*

**Ephesians 4:4-10**
*There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling; One Lord, one faith, one baptism, One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.

But unto every one of us is given grace according to the measure of the gift of Christ. Wherefore he saith, When he ascended up on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts unto men. (Now that he ascended, what is it but that he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth? He that descended is the same also that ascended up far above all heavens, that he might fill all things.)*

**Hebrews 2:14**
*Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil;*

In case anyone was wondering what "led captivity captive" means, here is the Biblical concept, first defined in Judges 5, as Deborah and Barak sing a victory prayer after they had defeated Israel's oppressors and made those kings and their nations who had enslaved them their slaves.

In a like manner, Jesus who was captive in Hell for 3 days and 3 nights, rose from the dead, bodily, led captivity captive, as He had victory and took power over death and Hell.

Misunderstanding what that phrase means has led many to believe false teachers who claim it means Jesus freed captives in Hell.

No. He freed mankind from the bonds of death and Hell. He took captive His captors.

teachings.title: Passover and the timing of the crucifixion
teachings.summary: Lines up the Passover week with Christ's triumphal entry, betrayal, crucifixion and resurrection, and argues that letting the Bible set the timing gives three days and three nights rather than the Good Friday tradition.
teachings.text:
I'm not 100% positive, but if today is Passover then we are aligned with the same schedule of events as the Passover of Jesus' crucifixion.

Saturday, His triumphant entry into Jerusalem, the 10th day of their month, Nisan. Tuesday night, the last supper and betrayal by Judas and arrest in the garden of Gethsemane. Today, brought before the High Priests, the lamb without blemish. Slain before the assembled people. Taken down from the cross and buried by 6PM tonight. Eventime. Three days and nights in Hell, three Sabbaths in a row, Passover, the first day of unleavened bread, Saturday. Risen on the first day of the week, Sunday.

Because our calendar isn't the same as the ancient Hebrews, and the lunar calendar and because they reckon days 6PM to 6PM, not at midnight as we do, it doesn't line up precisely each year.

One interesting note is that in the Talmud, according to the wicked Maimonides, Jews may never celebrate a passover on a Wednesday. (The timing given in the OT by God through Moses sets a specific date, regardless of timing).

Modern Jews use the Catholic tradition of claiming the Last Supper was a passover seder on Maundy Thursday to throw doubt on the Gospels. That, and the Good Friday narrative make it that the supper wasn't on Passover, and that Jesus would have only been dead one full day, Saturday, and possibly 2 nights under that formula, gives Jews ammunition to argue Jesus didn't fulfill the scriptures. That it was not 3 days and 3 nights, using the Catholic doctrine.

But of course it's their doctrine that's wrong, and when we allow the Bible to set the timing, we get to see just how the original passover and God's ordinance regarding it, and the other spring feasts, tie directly to Jesus. The foreshadowing of Christ. It is beautiful and perfect.

Another foolish argument comes from people who insist the modern calendar dates 33AD as having Jesus die on a Friday. Of course they are placing a man made calendar over the preserved and inspired word of God.

teachings.title: Neither will they be persuaded, though one rose
teachings.summary: In the rich man and Lazarus, those who will not hear Moses and the prophets would not believe even if one rose from the dead, as the hardened Jews proved.
teachings.text:
And it came to pass both died, and Lazarus went to Heaven, and the rich man to Hell.

And we are told that the rich man lifted up his eyes to heaven while in torment, and across the great gulf fixed between hell and Heaven saw Lazarus being comforted by father Abraham, and cried out for mercy. To send Lazarus with just a little water, a finger dipped, that his tongue would feel relief from the burning hellfire.

Where in life, Lazarus begged for his crumbs, the rich man is reduced to similar begging.

*But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented. And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.*

Daunted, and seeking place for repentance where none can be found, the rich man begs that Lazarus return to the land of the living and preach the truth of salvation to the rich man's brothers that they may be spared this fate.

*Abraham saith unto him, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.*

*And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent.*

*And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.*

Jesus makes the point emphatically. They didn't come to salvation by faith, which comes by hearing the word of God. They served Mammon, like the rich man in Hell. And just as they didn't believe Moses and the prophets, they wouldn't be persuaded though a man rose from the dead.

This has a double meaning, where there is the literal example of Lazarus, raised from the dead by Jesus in Bethany, whom the Jews saw come up from the grave after 4 days, made whole by the compassion of Jesus. And of course, Jesus speaks of His own looming death and resurrection. These vipers have hardened their hearts and wouldn't believe even if they saw the son of man rise again.

teachings.title: Strait is the gate, not difficult
teachings.summary: The strait gate is the one narrow way through Christ, and modern versions that make it difficult teach a hard salvation of works.
teachings.text:
Now Jesus has begun to make His way towards Jerusalem. His fate awaiting there, and He continues His mission, giving the Gospel to the poor that they may be redeemed.

A person asks if few will be saved, Jesus replies that we must enter in the strait gate, the narrow path, through Him. That many seek the kingdom but by the way that seems easy.

Similar passage to **Matthew 7:13-14**:
*Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat: because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.*

Modern false translations change the narrowness of the gate, the one path to salvation, to "difficult," teaching that salvation is hard and of works. But in the abbreviated telling in Luke the meaning is reinforced. Jesus is desperately trying to reach people with the truth, that they may turn towards God and be saved. The kingdom is nigh. Repent.

*When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath shut to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, Lord, open unto us; and he shall answer and say unto you, I know you not whence ye are: Then shall ye begin to say, We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets. But he shall say, I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity.*

Another parable warning then not to be shut out. Not to be like the virgins who didn't keep oil in their lamps, and when the bridegroom returned were shut out of the wedding feast. Like the wicked servant who abused his station while the master was away, only to be found out by the Lord's unexpected return. Not to be caught unawares like a thief coming in the night, but to be watchful and ready. Jesus preaches hellfire and brimstone. The destruction that awaits all men who do not come to believe.

*There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and you yourselves thrust out.*

teachings.title: Penance is not in scripture
teachings.summary: The word penance is not in scripture, and the Catholic NAB inserts it into Isaiah 58:5, a passage where God calls such practices sin.
teachings.text:
BTW, the term "penance" doesn't appear anywhere in scripture, even in the more corrupt modern versions, but Catholics draw their proof text from **Isaiah 58:5**, a chapter as we just saw that explicitly has God calling such practices sin.

The New American Bible (NAB), a popular Catholic perversion of the word, twists the scripture and changes "afflict [your] soul" to "penance": “Is this the manner of fasting I wish, of keeping a day of penance: That a man bow his head like a reed, and lie in sackcloth and ashes? Do you call this a fast, a day acceptable to the LORD?”

They don't even see the folly of using this, in its actual context, to justify the idea, or promote the yoke of abstinence and fasting, ashes and self- that God is literally telling Isaiah to preach against.

They take from it only that they were being insincere, not that God calls us to delight in His day of rest, to celebrate the sabbath we have in Christ, and do for others that He be glorified. Only that the Hebrews just went about self flagellation wrong.

teachings.title: Making a physical idol of spiritual pictures
teachings.summary: False teachers take parables and pictures literally out of context and build doctrines of devils on them, such as infant sprinkling, sacramental bread and wine and praying to saints.
teachings.text:
This study is the meat of the word, it's hard for many to digest. The vain traditions of those who claim Christ but teach their own wisdom, rejecting the word of God as the only authority and twisting scripture to defend their doctrines of devils, has beguiled many.

And so we are warned;

*Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels, intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind.*

(BTW, that goes for praying to dead "saints," as angels)

People take doctrine from out of context verses, or partial text, and using the logic of man, puffed up in their fleshly mind, work out by fallacious implications that their heretical doctrines are actually Biblical.

They fail to square plainly stated and often repeated clear doctrines that directly contradict their own. They take literal readings of parables that they don't understand, and apply their carnal mind to the Spirit.

They are like Nicodemus, the Pharisee who questioned Jesus in **John 3**, unable to understand the parables about being born twice, once of water from the womb, again in Spirit, reborn by faith.

 They become like the disciples offended by His parable in **John 6**, where He compares Himself to manna, bread come down from Heaven that we must "eat." They thought this was some sort of cannibalistic blasphemy, despite Jesus explaining "*It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.*"

Even today, many take parables and metaphors, pictures of the spiritual and make for themselves a physical idol of it. Missing the point.

And so you have denominations claiming to believe that salvation is by faith alone, still maintaining that sprinkling of infants and ritualistic eating of bread and drinking of wine bestows salvation, or keeps it. That works must be done to shore up that which is by faith alone. The contradictions lost on them, as is salvation.

teachings.title: It is written: resisting the devil by the word
teachings.summary: Jesus overcame Satan's temptations not by His divine nature but by clinging to every word of God, the pattern for how we resist temptation.
teachings.text:
Luke chapter 4 picks up with Jesus after His baptism in the Jordan and by the Holy Spirit, having been proclaimed by the Father "His Son, in whom Im well pleased."

The Gospel says, Jesus was led of the Spirit to the wilderness, and there to fast and be tempted by Satan, 40 days. It is often overlooked that the three instances given here and in the other Gospels are not the only tests of the devil Jesus suffered. He was tempted 40 days.

Jesus hungered. He thirst. He was weary. He was alone. Without shelter. Cold at night. Hot in the sun of the day. In all ways tempted as we are. But without sin.

And Jesus was led of the Spirit to this temptation, He was not given a pass, was not brought to the temple in Jerusalem to preach the Gospel to an adoring throng of people. He was brought to desolate places where the prince of this world would tempt Him.

Satan, the accuser of the brethren, seeking to corrupt the Christ, and derail God's plan of salvation for the world, tested and tried Jesus that he may go before the Father and say, "your Son is not worthy to be a sacrifice. He is not without blemish." But Jesus withstood Satan, and in doing so, gave us the pattern for dealing with temptation in our lives.

**1 Corinthians 10:13**
*There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.*

The Bible says Jesus was tempted as we are. Knows our infirmities and understanding, shows mercy on us. We are not given more than we can handle. If we reject Satan, God will provide us a way.

That way is found in what Jesus used to resist Satan. The word of God.

So understanding that Jesus did not have some special means to supernaturally avoid succumbing to sin, it wasn't His divine nature that saved His human flesh from falling, but His doing His Father's will, and clinging to the word.

Jesus was hungry and weak, and the devil said to turn a stone to bread. A temptation of the flesh. To satisfy the immediate need to please ourselves physically.

And Jesus replied *It is written, That man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.*

Note His use of "it is written." That man loves not by bread. Not by the needs of the flesh. That there is more to this than satisfying our physical desires but that we live by *every word of God*.

He quotes scripture to put of the devil from Him. Every word of God is all we need to live. (The presupposition is that, in order to be true, we have access to every word of God. Thus the preservation of His word). This having double meaning, as the manna in the desert was a picture of Christ, Jesus who is the bread of life come down from Heaven, and He is the Word of God made flesh, through whom eternal life is given to all who believe.

And Jesus, using God's word, rebukes Satan.

Then, tempting Jesus with power, Satan offers Him the thrones of this world, of whom Satan is god. Given power to influence kings and regents. The spirits that bring wickedness to high places. Overseeing the principalities of the rulers of the darkness of this world. By supernatural means, he takes Jesus to the top of a mountain and shows Him all the lands of man in the world. The devil says to Jesus, worship me and I will give you an earthly kingdom, ultimate power.

And Jesus, again citing scripture rejects him; *for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.* And again the power of the knowledge of God's word saves Jesus from temptation.

Finally, frustrated, Satan places Jesus upon the spire of the temple in Jerusalem. Hundreds of feet in the air. And says to jump, because the scriptures say that God the Father would not suffer to see even His foot dash against the rocks. That God would send angels to stop Jesus from even stubbing His toe, so surely they would catch Him.

*And Jesus answering said unto him, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.*

teachings.title: The Trumpets Are Wrath, Not Tribulation
teachings.summary: The trumpet judgments are God's wrath fuelled by the saints' prayers and cannot be confused with the tribulation, and Revelation is meant to reveal.
teachings.text:
God's wrath, the trumpets of war, sounding 7 times (similar to the battle of Jericho where they sounded trumpets 7 times around the city). Only 4 in, and so far there is massive destruction. Unnatural natural disasters. This is the wrath of God fueled by the prayers of the saints. It cannot be confused with the tribulation, even that great tribulation that came just prior to the day of the Lord.

When we get to the second half of the book of Revelation, we will see the 7 vial judgments which, when compared to the 7 trumpet judgments, we will see they are complimentary, in how they affect the earth and its remaining inhabitants, and in their timing. (Chapters 12-22 retell much of 1-11, from a different vantage point, with added details)

It is important to see how things progress, and how the timing is consistent with other scripture that talks about end times Bible prophecy, and just how clear the things stated are. We may see through a glass darkly, but we are given quite a lot of details and signs to watch for, and an order of things that is clear when taken in context. God is not the author of confusion. Revelation means to reveal, not to obscure.

teachings.title: Revelation Is Written to Reveal
teachings.summary: Revelation is a blessing written to reveal, and its late first century authorship by John undoes the preterist claim that it was fulfilled in 70 AD.
teachings.text:
The revelation of Jesus Christ as told to John, signified by His angel, written to Jesus' servants, and directly to the 7 churches which were in Asia, to tell us the things which John had seen, which are and things which shall be hereafter.

The book of Jesus Christ's Revelation is not written to obscure. Its intent is literally the title. To reveal. Those of us saved by Christ are blessed by reading it. Hearing it. Keeping the prophecy of those things written therein, for the time is at hand.

Written in the late first century, likely around 93AD, by the Apostle John, who served Jesus in His earthly ministry with his brother James, who was martyred shortly after Christ's ascent. Called by Jesus "Boanerges," or the "sons of thunder," their mother asked Jesus for favor for her sons in **Matthew 20:20-28**.

John was the apostle Jesus loved, who wrote the Gospel and epistles.

Now, exiled to Patmos by Domitian, emperor of Rome from 81 to 96AD, for, as John writes here; "*for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus Christ."* We know the timing and details from John's disciple, Polycarp, and early texts by historians Clement of Alexandria, Victorinus, Eusebius and Jerome.

The timing of its writing doesn't much matter for us, blessed readers. The earthly things are incidental to spiritual. But the heresy of preterism requires the authorship to be pre-70AD, because it relies on the early writing to make the desolation of Judah by Rome, the destruction of the temple and murder and scattering of the Jews, serve as fulfilment of the prophecy.

Other modern "scholars" cast doubt on the author's identity, deny John wrote Revelation, often claiming different people wrote the Gospel, epistles and Revelation attributed to John, however the style and description of spiritual things by the Apostle, as well as the clearly inspired truth contained put that heresy to bed sufficiently for believers. That John's peers and ancient historians testify that it was his bolsters that, but a careful reading of scripture is all we really need.

teachings.title: A literal creation about 6,000 years ago
teachings.summary: Genesis 1 is a literal account of creation about 6,200 years ago because God who cannot lie says so, and evolution is worship of time, a created thing.
teachings.text:
Now, note the order of things. This is how all of creation was made. And the creation of days, separated from night, morning and evening, was created by God who is outside of time.

The fullness of the Godhead exists when nothing else did, including time, and through Him was created light, substance, life, and mankind. Everything after its own kind, with the seed contained therein propagating that life over time.

This is a literal story of creation, as it occurred roughly 6,200 years ago.

Not because of fossils found in weird places, or the problems with carbon dating, or the position of the stars in the firmament unchanging, or the complexity and variance of life.

But because God said this is how it happened. In His inspired and preserved word, The God who cannot lie tells us these things and that they are so.

Evolution, which is the worship of time, or Kronos as the creator, is literally the worship of the created, as we see in Genesis, because God created time. And so we know it's false.

Biblical inerrancy, and the fundamentalist belief that it is the inspired and preserved word of God, has yet to fail, even as science falsely so-called makes claims to the contrary, God's hand is revealed continually making the wise into fools.

This is why God's word is continually under attack. This is why doubt is continually sown. Because, if many have doubts about any aspect of God's word, then many will not believe the report. The Gospel, and will perish as sinners.

And while you don't have to necessarily believe in the literal biblical creation in order to believe that Jesus is the son of God who died for our sins and was resurrected again, and whom through which we are given Grace by God unto eternal life, it is difficult to then express that Faith to others while doubting much of His word. Or thinking it allegory, or some sort of parable.

The gospels give account back to Adam. The genealogies are there to mark time. And the generations from Noah back to Adam, from Abraham back to Noah, from Israel to Christ... These are there for a purpose.

And while there are some seeking to take away from God's word by casting doubt not just on the creation story but on every biblical text that draws upon it, all scripture that refers to it in describing Jesus Christ to us, there are people that seek to add to his word as well. It is easy to read into it things that are not there, and this too is an error.

So as we go forth through Genesis understand that it is not only the faith of this author, but my firm opinion that the Bible is literally true, and the truths revealed from Genesis 1 through the end in Revelation 22, is the story of Jesus Christ. God revealing His Son to us that we may believe and have eternal life.

It is God's word, His testimony, the testaments that He has given us to His promise for us. And from start to finish, Alpha to Omega it is one gospel, the good news of salvation through Christ Jesus.

teachings.title: The sower: deep roots in good ground
teachings.summary: Jesus used natural things to teach the spiritual, which the natural man cannot discern, and saved believers can be stony or thorny ground unless they grow deep roots in God's word.
teachings.text:
In Mark 4 we see another parallel passage, this time with Matthew 13 which we studied a few weeks ago. (it's repeated in **Luke 8** as well, which God willing we shall see soon)

The parable of the sower is another instance of the nature of creation existing that Jesus, the word of God though whom all things were created, may use it as example to explain the heavenly things of God. The physical to understand the spiritual.

For we who are saved, the greater lesson is how we rightly divide the word, understanding that His words are spirit. That His words are eternal life, and what that means. That creation speaks the word of God for those with ears to hear and eyes to see. Who aren't without deep roots, who aren't choked out by thorns. That we may be fertile soil and bring forth fruit after our kind, 100 fold.

*And he said unto them, Unto you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God: but unto them that are without, all these things are done in parables: That seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest at any time they should be converted, and their sins should be forgiven them*.

Jesus used clearly discerned pictures of the natural, the physical, to help us understand the spiritual, the unseen, that we who are seeking God's truth or who have received the quickening of our spirit may receive faith, which the Bible says *is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.*

He uses the seen to give us insight to the unseen. This is what I was getting at yesterday.

But to the carnally minded all things are physical, literal. Materialists see Jesus parables as Nicodemus did; taken to absurd levels or autistic literalism and missing the actual spiritual application.

This is what the Bible means by "*the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned."*

The natural man is earthly. They rely on the wisdom of man. They lean unto their own understanding. They are those by the wayside where the word is sown and *Satan cometh immediately, and taketh* it away.

And as we see in the parable of the sower, as Jesus explains, there are saved Christians who are the stoney ground. They hear the word and believe, but having nothing to take hold of, being unprofitable, without a church, without reading their Bible, without seeking to learn the deeper things of God, *and so endure but for a time: afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word's sake, immediately they are offended.*

There are Christians who hear the word and are saved, but are among thorns, the cares of the world. They allow covetousness and lust to choke them out, and become unable to bear fruit. To get more people saved by their example. Unprofitable to God or to others.

We should seek to grow roots, deep in fertile soil which is God's word and His ways that we may win souls to Christ and bring in the harvest for the Lord.

teachings.title: To him that hath shall more be given
teachings.summary: God gives understanding freely to those who receive His word, but from hardened hearts by the wayside He eventually takes the light away.
teachings.text:
The lesson of why Jesus uses parables, and the true nature of creation to serve as that parable is given us that we may receive more. That having been given eternal life, and having been made alive in the spirit, we may be given yet more.

It's the opposite of gnosticism, where the secrets are revealed by measures, and final "enlightenment" kept hidden until one archives the ability to see.

The Bible way is that we seeking enlightenment are given it immediately, if we believe God's word. Then our knowledge grows the more we receive it, freely given. The light put on a candlestick, not hidden under a bushel.

It's not hid from those who ask. It's freely given *with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you: and unto you that hear shall more be given.*

It's up to you if you be stoney ground. It's up to you if you allow thorns to choke you out. It's up to you if you be fertile soil. What you ask for is what you're given, to those that hear.

*For he that hath, to him shall be given: and he that hath not, from him shall be taken even that which he hath.*

He that hath not, those without ears to hear, those by the wayside, they are given the chance to receive the word. The seed is sown in their hearts. But even this is taken away eventually. God doesn't shine His light on all men forever. The Spirit tries for a time, but if you don't want to hear the truth, if the seed can't spring up on your hardened heart, compacted like the well-worn soil of the pathway by the wayside, He will take His light away to shine on more fertile hearts. Then it is too late.

teachings.title: Judas repented, yet went to his own place
