teachings.summary: Judas repented of betraying innocent blood yet was damned, showing that repenting of a wrong is not believing on Christ, which is why modern versions change repented to remorse.
teachings.text:
As the lamb without blemish is led away by the chief priests to Pilate, we are told Judas Iscariot, who had betrayed Christ for 30 pieces of silver, repented, changed his mind, thought better of what he'd done, and saying, *I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood.*

**Psalms 41:9** - *Yea, mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me.*

**Zechariah 11:12** - *And I said unto them, If ye think good, give me my price; and if not, forbear. So they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver.*

Judas, rebuffed by the priests of the temple, and unable to come to salvation having been damned by his rejection of the truth, hanged himself, and the 30 pieces of silver used to buy a potters field for the graves of strangers.

**Luke 22:22** *For the Son of man indeed goeth, as it hath been determined: but woe unto that man through whom he is betrayed!*

Repenting of a wrong done doesn't equate with believing on Christ for salvation.

Jesus said to His Apostles, of Judas "*Have not I chosen you twelve, and one of you is a devil?”*

And as he hanged himself, the Bible tells us the details of his fate;

**Acts 1:18** *Now this man purchased a field with the reward of iniquity; and falling headlong, he burst asunder in the midst, and all his bowels gushed out.*

*19 And it was known unto all the dwellers at Jerusalem; insomuch as that field is called in their proper tongue, Aceldama, that is to say, The field of blood.*

*20 For it is written in the book of Psalms, Let his habitation be desolate, and let no man dwell therein: and his bishoprick let another take.*

*21 Wherefore of these men which have companied with us all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us,*

*22 Beginning from the baptism of John, unto that same day that he was taken up from us, must one be ordained to be a witness with us of his resurrection.*

*23 And they appointed two, Joseph called Barsabas, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias.*

*24 And they prayed, and said, Thou, Lord, which knowest the hearts of all men, shew whether of these two thou hast chosen,*

*25 That he may take part of this ministry and apostleship, from which Judas by transgression fell, that he might go to his own place.*

"His own place" being a euphemism for Hell, a place man earns for himself, (as opposed to Heaven by which no man can earn their way in to possess).

I will note that in modern translations, they remove the word "repented" here, and replace it with "felt remorse," because the idea that Judas repented would conflict with the false teaching of turning from sin to be saved, rather than faith in Christ, and it would lead people to question if Judas repented, if he is in Heaven. Again, reminding us that bad doctrine begets bad doctrine and confusion. And they have to further change God's word to take on new meaning to support it.

teachings.title: The last days and the Olivet question
teachings.summary: We have been in the last days since the Ascension, and the temple's destruction is a separate prophecy from Christ's coming, which dispensationalists and preterists both mix up.
teachings.text:
The idea of dual fulfillment, and a definitions of what constitutes the end times has long been a contentious point.

**2 Peter 3** addresses this, that even in that first century:

*Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts,And saying, Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation.*

Peter goes on to warn against those casting doubts regarding the kingdom to come and the resurrection, who took prophecy as singular, and allegorical, and used that point of view to undermine the faith in the Kingdom promised us in Christ.

According to **Colossians 1:5-6**, the gospel has been preached to the whole world, even at that time. And as Peter notes, and is referenced in other Epistles, the last days have come following the Ascension of Christ. We are living in the end times, and have for 2,000 years if the calendar is to be believed.

What triggered Jesus' discourse was the Apostles wondering at the buildings of the temple, and Jesus prophesying that it would be destroyed, not one stone left upon another. It is after this that they privately ask Jesus, "*Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world*?"

Dispensationalists and others will take the destruction of the temple and add it to the prophecy that follows regarding His second coming and the end of the world, when it is a separate prophecy that spurred the broader discussion.

Preterists will take the same approach, but say all things were fulfilled in 70AD with its destruction.

But fundamentalists, reading in the spirit can see the order of how this is presented in Matthew 24. Rightly dividing the word of God.

teachings.title: Verses misused for repenting of sin
teachings.summary: Ezekiel 14, Luke 13 and Revelation 9, rightly divided, are about national judgment, misunderstanding, and unbelief, not repenting of sins to be born again.
teachings.text:
It's easy to understand, by looking at verses commonly cited as supporting the false damnable heresy of repentance of sin for salvation, to see precisely what is being repented of in each.

Ezekiel 14:6

*Therefore say unto the house of Israel, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Repent, and turn yourselves from your idols; and turn away your faces from all your abominations.*

First, let us rightly divide the word of God here, it isn't regarding salvation of a person's soul, rather this is directed at the nation of Israel which had put their faith in idols, facing the abominations set before them in service to false gods.

God speaking through the prophet is telling them that they will be judged as a nation if they do not repent of false belief in idols.

Or **Luke 13**

*There were present at that season some that told him of the Galilaeans, whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices.*

*2 And Jesus answering said unto them, Suppose ye that these Galilaeans were sinners above all the Galilaeans, because they suffered such things?*

*3 I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.*

*4 Or those eighteen, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and slew them, think ye that they were sinners above all men that dwelt in Jerusalem?*

*5 I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.*

*6 He spake also this parable; A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard; and he came and sought fruit thereon, and found none.*

*7 Then said he unto the dresser of his vineyard, Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none: cut it down; why cumbereth it the ground?*

*8 And he answering said unto him, Lord, let it alone this year also, till I shall dig about it, and dung it:*

*9 And if it bear fruit, well: and if not, then after that thou shalt cut it down.*

Jesus isn't telling them to repent of their sins, he's reminding them that they are as sinful as those they are judging. That people who have suffered a bitter end, in this case being killed by Pilate or in a construction accident were no more or less sinners than they were. And they need to repent of that misunderstanding of how things work, because it is a stumbling block to their acceptance of salvation.

**Revelation 9**

*20 And the rest of the men which were not killed by these plagues yet repented not of the works of their hands, that they should not worship devils, and idols of gold, and silver, and brass, and stone, and of wood: which neither can see, nor hear, nor walk:*

*21 Neither repented they of their murders, nor of their sorceries, nor of their fornication, nor of their thefts.*

Again, this verse isn't about individual soul salvation. What we are witnessing is God's wrath pouring out on the unbelievers that remained on the Earth, and that despite all the horrors being poured out upon them, including the plague of hellish locust creatures, the unbelieving didn't repent of their unbelief, they didn't turn from their idols or their wickedness to be saved, physically from the wrath.

Using these three instances as an example of repenting of your sins to be born again, shows a lack of spiritual discernment and understanding of scripture. Don't be fooled.

teachings.title: The falling away first, and the corrupt versions
teachings.summary: 2 Thessalonians 2 says the falling away and the man of sin come before the day of Christ, and modern versions that turn the falling away into rebellion and lawlessness set believers up to be seen as the rebels against the antichrist.
teachings.text:
Just touching on this theme: The push for false Christianity that places salvation under the law, not under grace, the Noahide false religion, Hebrew Roots, Lordship/Repenting of sin, Judaizing, etc...is meant to bring about the falling away of believers, and pave the way for the antichrist and his false claim of being Jesus, returned.

*3 Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition;*

That believers who oppose the antichrist, who they will hail as Christ, and our rebelling against him, being against the law as a means of salvation, etc, we would be seen as the "bad guys" by these false believers under the beast's delusion, and the fraudulent Bible versions used to reinforce it to persecute those of us under grace.

teachings.title: The leaven of the Pharisees is their doctrine
teachings.summary: Jesus uses bread for the word and leaven for false doctrine, and natural men who take it literally turn it into a materialistic cannibal sacrament.
teachings.text:
Matthew 16, the chapter that contains the one half-sentence, stripped of all context and twisted into blasphemy, that Catholics use to justify the false church's existence.

It is an interesting chapter, serving as a transition for Jesus' earthly ministry from service to the masses, finding the lost sheep, to preparing for the end, the death burial and resurrection.

It begins as most of Matthew, with a short story of Pharisees and Sadducees and scribes, coming to Jesus and attempting to trap Him or trick Him with leading questions, this time again asking Jesus to perform some kind of sign, and again He rebukes them that they should see the sign of the times all around them, but perceiving not the things of God, the only sign that will be given them is the sign of Jonas, signifying His approaching fate and triumphant resurrection following 3 days and 3 nights in Hell.

And, as throughout Matthew, Jesus takes the opportunity to preach, here teaching His Apostles, saying beware the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees. The apostles, who we are told were focused on their forgetting bread for the journey, questioned if He was talking about actual bread, literal food, and their lack of it. Jesus reproaching them to focus on what He's teaching, spiritual things, and to not worry about he material. Didn't He just feed thousands, repeatedly, with physical bread? He wants them to focus on the spiritual aspect of His parable.

*How is it that ye do not understand that I spake it not to you concerning bread, that ye should beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees? Then understood they how that he bade them not beware of the leaven of bread, but of the doctrine of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.*

Jesus repeatedly uses bread as an allegory for the word of God, for scripture and for doctrine being taught. The daily wisdom from God's word we are to pray for. The bread from Heaven that if we should eat, never hunger again. That gives eternal life. It is spiritual, not actual wheat and water. And the leaven, which often represents sin in these parables, is the false teaching and doctrines of the Pharisees and Sadducees, which infecting the "lump," the "dough" of proper doctrine, will grow and spread, corrupting it.

Natural man misunderstanding, making Jesus' parables using bread as imagery, cannot grasp that He is speaking of spiritual things, of God and His doctrine. That man lives not by bread alone but by every word of the living God. That Jesus, like mana, is the the bread to come down from Heaven, giving eternal life to all who partake in it. That the flesh profits nothing, that this is spiritual.

And, lacking discernment, the natural man proceeds to turn what is an eloquent teaching moment preached to us by the Son of God, into a materialistic cannibal-cult ritual. That little leaven of misunderstanding infecting the whole lump with its yeast, and creating a worldly sacrament that people put their faith in rather than the word of God.

teachings.title: William Tyndale and the English Bible
teachings.summary: Recounts how Tyndale printed the first English New Testament in 1526, with more than 90 percent of it matching the later King James Version. Notes that the Roman Catholic Church had him strangled and burned and burned his first edition.
teachings.text:

teachings.title: Primary doctrine and incidental opinions
teachings.summary: Says a belief is not Biblical doctrine unless scripture clearly spells it out, separating primary doctrines such as literal creation from secondary matters like the exact age of the earth. Urges not becoming dogmatic over the firmament or other worldly things, and hearing sound doctrine from preachers who hold the gospel of grace alone.
teachings.text:
Just because you believe something about the world to be true, doesn't make it Biblical doctrine. It actually has to be clearly spelled out in scripture, and even then other than the Gospel and a few primary doctrines, there's interpretation of secondary and tertiary doctrine that's open for discussion and then there are things people try to get the Bible to comment on that it simply doesn't.

Literal creation is a primary doctrine. Biblical age as determined by generations is secondary. Earth being precisely 6,482 years old is interpretation that has Biblical basis, but is incidental, bearing no real importance in our spiritual walk, and good faith people of faith can disagree.

Too many place their own beliefs of incidental and worldly things far too high in the order of importance.

Many, many, many of the people in our circles, especially young men who are aimless, lost, broken by trauma, or babes in Christ and culturally Christian but not quite there yet, need to hear hard preaching on sin and practical application of Biblical truths to their spiritual life and walk with Christ, from preachers who adhere to the Gospel of salvation by faith alone, in grace alone, plus nothing, minus nothing.

And that preacher's idea or opinion of worldly things differing from your own shouldn't be a hindrance from hearing sound doctrine of spiritual things.

If it is, you need to reevaluate what's important to you.

My preference for Easton's definition of Firmament in the Bible, over Nave's or Smith's, or even Webster's, doesn't make it doctrine. Simple as.

It could just be the expanse, the reach of the heavens. "Firm" being in the word doesn't make it solid, even if I believe it to be.

Don't project your opinions of the worldly onto scripture and become dogmatic in things that are ultimately not important.

Sons of Belial, Jews and reprobates, being liars and leading persecution and engaging in subversion is true, because the Bible tells us so, explicitly. We don't have to prove they lie about the shape of the earth, or space, or age of creation, etc to prove they lie. Examples are simply signs to read, and the truth to ponder and wonder about.

teachings.title: James 2 is no snare for works salvation
teachings.summary: Read in context and compared with the rest of scripture, James 2 is written to the already saved and its rhetorical questions cannot overturn the clear doctrine that we are made righteous by faith alone.
teachings.text:
Now we come to the verses that are a snare to so many, where they justify works based righteousness, despite all of the mountain of scripture that assures us we are made righteous by faith alone, through grace alone, in the perfect work of Christ Jesus.

But, comparing scripture with scripture, and the verses in context, it's not difficult to understand, unless you're a natural man seeking to force the Bible to fit your preconceived notion, rather than letting it tell you God's.

First, what follows is a series of rhetorical questions and reasoning logic, designed to give example to what James has already preached. And again, it is written to the brethren, the author assumes it is to those already saved, to exhort and edify, not to get them to believe. Not to save them spiritually, but to those already saved, become more complete in their Christian life.

We do not receive doctrine from rhetorical questions or "a man may say..." reasoning, stripped of context. We get them from clear statements that do not contradict others.

For brevity sake I have already given argument above, with verses as to why this interpretation that we must do works to be able to go to heaven and have eternal life is damnable heresy. Scroll up. I may add to it as we study through this section, but if that's not sufficient for you, your argument is with God, the Gospel as given by Jesus and then shared by the Apostles, and clear, consistent verses, given again and again from Genesis to Revelation.

If you are trusting in your own works to get righteous or to maintain the righteousness given by God in Christ, you are damning yourself and being made debtor to the whole of the law which no one can keep perfectly. For there are none righteous no not one. Repent, and obey the Gospel.

teachings.title: The sign of the prophet Jonas
teachings.summary: The tomb was empty before dawn Sunday after three full days and nights, fulfilling the sign of Jonas, and getting this timing wrong opens the door to worse error about Christ's suffering.
teachings.text:
Now, the first day of the week in the Bible is what we call Sunday. This finishes establishing the timeline of Jesus' death, burial and resurrection. Following 3days and nights, *before* dawn Sunday morning, Mary comes and the tomb is empty, Christ has risen already. The "night" is not yet "over," being yet dark. Wednesday night, Thursday night, Friday night. Thursday, Friday, Saturday.

*But he answered and said unto them, An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas: For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.*
...
*Then Jonah prayed unto the Lord his God out of the fish's belly, And said, I cried by reason of mine affliction unto the Lord, and he heard me; out of the belly of hell cried I, and thou heardest my voice.*
*For thou hadst cast me into the deep, in the midst of the seas; and the floods compassed me about: all thy billows and thy waves passed over me.*
*Then I said, I am cast out of thy sight; yet I will look again toward thy holy temple.The waters compassed me about, even to the soul: the depth closed me round about, the weeds were wrapped about my head. I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; the earth with her bars was about me for ever: yet hast thou brought up my life from corruption, O Lord my God. When my soul fainted within me I remembered the Lord: and my prayer came in unto thee, into thine holy temple.*
*They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy. But I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that that I have vowed. Salvation is of the Lord.*

It's a minor doctrine, the timing of these things, and yet its corruption and basic misunderstanding lead to all kinds of heresy and error. The day of the week isn't really important, but what Jesus did in that time is.

Often false teachers will use misunderstanding and error to build other, more damnable doctrine. Such as Jesus didn't suffer in Hell as a burnt offering for sin. Such as He didn't do so for 3 days and nights as the Bible says, making some doubt scripture.

Nothing in the Bible is incidental, accidental or coincidental. All scripture is valuable for doctrine.

teachings.title: No verse says quit sin to be saved
teachings.summary: There is no clear verse making giving up sin a condition of salvation, so it is not doctrine, since doctrine must come from clear scripture, not men.
teachings.text:
This quick bible study on the concept of repentance in the Bible isn't exhaustive however, it is conclusive. There is no clear verse that spells out a Doctrine that says that we must give up sin or be willing to give up sin in order to believe and be saved. Repentance is a changing of mind or turning from one thing to another.

I left out the verses where it says God repented. No one would say God repented of his sin because God is sinless.

And as I'm trying to express in this channel when dealing with mistaken ideas, error, and damnable heresies, unless you have a clear verse that says precisely what it is you're saying as Doctrine, that doesn't contradict anything else in the Bible, then it's wrong.

We get our Doctrine from scripture, not men.

teachings.title: The Spirit reproves the world of sin: because they believe not on Me
teachings.summary: Reads John 16:7-11 and notes the KJV word is reprove, not convict, and that the sin named is not believing on Jesus. Warns that the newer versions' wording opens the door to repent-of-your-sin works salvation.
teachings.text:
**John 16:7-11**

*7 Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you.

8 And when he is come, he will **reprove** the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment:

9 Of sin, because they believe not on me;

10 Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more;

11 Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged*.

Public Service Announcement: In false new age versions, they use "convict" rather than the precise term, "reprove" in this verse, so they can insert the false doctrine of "repent-of-your-sin" works salvation. Don't be fooled!

When Jesus says the Holy Spirit will reprove for sin, note what the sin is; not believing on Him.
